text: CXGBoost R6 class fits two-head XGBoost outcome model (optional propensity model via ranger). Key arguments CXGBoost: parameters: List XGBoost hyperparameters (e.g. eta, max_depth, lambda, alpha, tree_method). Defaults include num_target = 2, multi_strategy = "multi_output_tree". $fit(X, t, y, nrounds, verbose, eval_data): X = covariate matrix (NAs median-imputed), t = binary treatment (0/1), y = observed outcome; nrounds = boosting rounds (default 100); optional eval_data watchlist verbose >= 1. $predict(X): Returns list y0_hat, y1_hat, tau_hat, propensity_score. $summary(), $evaluate(y_true, X), $plot_importance(), $save_model(path), load_cxgboost(path), $clone_reset(): see Implementation R section . Sample ATE training set (mean predicted CATE). predict() output includes tau_hat convenience. ATE average treatment effect logged gonorrhea rate (lnr) across training population—.e., much early repeal abortion prohibition associated change lnr.
code: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Model Configuration and Training # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- model_params <- list(   max_depth = 5,   eta = 1e-2,           # learning_rate   nrounds = 100,         # n_estimators (passed to fit())   nthread = -1,          # n_jobs = -1 (use all cores)   lambda = 5,   alpha = 1.0,           # reg_alpha   # reg_lambda in Python is lambda above   tree_method = "hist" )  nrounds <- model_params$nrounds model_params$nrounds <- NULL  # fit() takes nrounds separately  cx_model <- CXGBoost$new(parameters = model_params) cx_model$fit(X_train, W_train, Y_train, nrounds = nrounds, verbose = 0L) cx_model$summary() CXGBoost  Model Summary    Configuration    eta (learning rate)  : 0.0100   max_depth            : 5   subsample            : 0.80   colsample_bytree     : 0.80   lambda (L2)          : 5.00   alpha  (L1)          : 1.00   Boosting rounds      : two_boosters    Fit time             : 0.30 sec   Propensity Model    Ranger OOB error     : 0.0575   Ranger num.trees     : 200   Ranger max.depth     : 4   Top 10 Variables (XGBoost gain)    income       0.3360     totpop       0.2834     ur           0.1846     alcohol      0.0747     ir           0.0648     crack        0.0306     poverty      0.0259 pred_train <- cx_model$predict(X_train) ate_train_est <- mean(pred_train$tau_hat) cat("Training sample ATE (mean CATE):", round(ate_train_est, 4), "\n") Training sample ATE (mean CATE): -0.6037

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Prediction (returns y0_hat, y1_hat, tau_hat, propensity_score) # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- pred_test <- cx_model$predict(X_test) predicted_potential_outcomes <- cbind(pred_test$y0_hat, pred_test$y1_hat) cate_test_pred <- pred_test$tau_hat hist(cate_test_pred, main = "CATE Distribution (Test Set)", xlab = "Estimated Treatment Effect (lnr)", col = "lightblue")

RCausalML package provides R6 class CXGBoost $fit(), $predict() (returning y0_hat, y1_hat, tau_hat, propensity_score), $summary(), $evaluate(y_true, X), $plot_importance(), $save_model() / load_cxgboost(), $clone_reset(), plus exported PEHE() ATE() (matrix vector form) evaluation ground-truth potential outcomes exist. tutorial demonstrated fitting C-XGBoost synthetic data abortion dataset causaldata, including data preprocessing, training, CATE prediction, sample ATE, variable importance via $plot_importance(), propensity scores built-ranger model. tutorial covered core concepts, implementation details, evaluation workflow C-XGBoost R. advanced use cases (e.g., RATE/AUTOC, doubly-robust extensions, multiclass potential outcomes), additional methods packages may needed. encourage readers explore reference implementation related literature deeper understanding experimentation.

C-XGBoost: two-head XGBoost treatment masking causal inference (see package R/causalXGBoost.R C-XGBoost reference implementation). DragonNet-style outcome regression: Shi et al., “Adapting Neural Networks Estimation Treatment Effects” (2019). causal forests RATE/AUTOC R, see {grf} package (Athey, Tibshirani, Wager; Annals Statistics, 2019).

Boosted IV Forest (Instrumental Causal XGBoost) machine learning method combines cross-fitted C-XGBoost nuisance estimation Generalized Random Forests (GRF) instrumental forest estimate conditional local average treatment effects (LATE) presence endogeneity. uses XGBoost flexibly estimate \(E[Y|X]\), \(E[W|X]\), \(E[Z|X]\), residualises outcome, treatment, instrument, fits instrumental forest residuals—delivering robust, heterogeneous LATE estimates valid instrument available. Boosted IV Forest estimates heterogeneous treatment effects settings treatment assignment endogenous — , correlated unobserved factors also affect outcome. Like standard Instrumental Forest, exploits instrumental variable \(Z\) shifts treatment \(W\) without directly affecting outcome \(Y\). “boosted” part refers nuisance functions estimated: rather using regression forests first stage, uses C-XGBoost (two-head XGBoost) inside cross-fitting pipeline, enabling flexible capture nonlinearities interactions. second stage remains standard grf::instrumental_forest, preserving GRF’s interpretability, honest estimation, asymptotically valid confidence intervals. result two-stage estimator combines best worlds: XGBoost’s strength tabular data first stage, GRF’s principled causal inference machinery second. quantity interest Conditional Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) — treatment effect compliers (units whose treatment status changes \(Z\)), allowed vary covariates: \[\tau(X) = \frac{\text{Cov}[Y - \hat{m}(X),\; Z - \hat{p}(X) \mid X]}{\text{Cov}[W - \hat{e}(X),\; Z - \hat{p}(X) \mid X]}\] three nuisance functions : \(\hat{m}(X) = E[Y \mid X]\) — conditional mean outcome, estimated partial baseline variation \(Y\); \(\hat{e}(X) = E[W \mid X]\) — treatment propensity, estimated partial selection treatment; \(\hat{p}(X) = E[Z \mid X]\) — instrument propensity, estimated partial covariate-driven variation \(Z\). residualizing, numerator \(\text{Cov}[\tilde{Y}, \tilde{Z} \mid X]\) captures much instrument moves outcome; denominator \(\text{Cov}[\tilde{W}, \tilde{Z} \mid X]\) captures much instrument moves treatment. ratio isolates local causal effect \(W\) \(Y\) — purged confounding — complier subpopulation covariates \(X = x\). standard instrumental forest estimates \(\hat{m}\), \(\hat{e}\), \(\hat{p}\) using regression forests (skips nuisance estimation entirely instrument assumed randomized). works well nuisance functions smooth additive, can underfit outcomes treatments depend complex interactions covariates. Replacing first stage cross-fitted C-XGBoost addresses directly: XGBoost captures irregular boundaries, high-order interactions, nonlinear feature effects regression forests can miss. Like standard Instrumental Forest, exploits instrumental variable \(Z\) shifts treatment \(W\) without directly affecting outcome \(Y\). “boosted” part refers nuisance functions estimated: rather using regression forests first stage, uses C-XGBoost (two-head XGBoost) inside cross-fitting pipeline, enabling flexible capture nonlinearities interactions. second stage remains standard grf::instrumental_forest, preserving GRF’s interpretability, honest estimation, asymptotically valid confidence intervals. result two-stage estimator combines best worlds: XGBoost’s strength tabular data first stage, GRF’s principled causal inference machinery second. quantity interest Conditional Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) — treatment effect compliers (units whose treatment status changes \(Z\)), allowed vary covariates: \[\tau(X) = \frac{\text{Cov}[Y - \hat{m}(X),\; Z - \hat{p}(X) \mid X]}{\text{Cov}[W - \hat{e}(X),\; Z - \hat{p}(X) \mid X]}\] three nuisance functions : \(\hat{m}(X) = E[Y \mid X]\) — conditional mean outcome, estimated partial baseline variation \(Y\); \(\hat{e}(X) = E[W \mid X]\) — treatment propensity, estimated partial selection treatment; \(\hat{p}(X) = E[Z \mid X]\) — instrument propensity, estimated partial covariate-driven variation \(Z\). residualizing, numerator \(\text{Cov}[\tilde{Y}, \tilde{Z} \mid X]\) captures much instrument moves outcome; denominator \(\text{Cov}[\tilde{W}, \tilde{Z} \mid X]\) captures much instrument moves treatment. ratio isolates local causal effect \(W\) \(Y\) — purged confounding — complier subpopulation covariates \(X = x\). standard instrumental forest estimates \(\hat{m}\), \(\hat{e}\), \(\hat{p}\) using regression forests (skips nuisance estimation entirely instrument assumed randomized). works well nuisance functions smooth additive, can underfit outcomes treatments depend complex interactions covariates. Replacing first stage cross-fitted C-XGBoost addresses directly: XGBoost captures irregular boundaries, high-order interactions, nonlinear feature effects regression forests can miss. Cross-fitting (k-fold --sample prediction) prevents nuisance estimates overfitting training data, otherwise inflate apparent signal residuals bias second-stage LATE estimates. second stage remains unchanged — grf::instrumental_forest residualized \((\tilde{Y}, \tilde{W}, \tilde{Z}, X)\) — improvement surgical: better nuisances, inference. theoretical justification Neyman orthogonality GRF moment condition: LATE estimator locally insensitive small errors nuisance estimation, meaning flexible first-stage models improve finite-sample performance without introducing asymptotic bias, long nuisances converge reasonable rate. Boosted IV Forest inherits standard IV assumptions: Relevance — \(Z\) must strong predictor \(W\) conditional \(X\). Weak instruments inflate variance \(\tau(X)\) can cause severe bias; implementation reports first-stage F-statistic issues weak-instrument warnings. Exclusion restriction — \(Z\) affects \(Y\) \(W\), direct path. testable data must justified domain knowledge. K-fold cross-fitting breaks feedback loop ensuring every nuisance prediction made --sample. theoretical grounding Neyman orthogonality: IV moment condition locally insensitive small errors \(\hat{m}\), \(\hat{e}\), \(\hat{p}\), cross-fitted nuisances moderate convergence rate sufficient root-\(n\) inference \(\tau(X)\). Step 3 two methods meet. residuals \((\tilde{Y}, \tilde{W}, \tilde{Z})\) carry variation attributable treatment effect heterogeneity — confounding signal explained \(X\) subtracted. dimnames(mu_hat)[[2]]   outcomes <- dimnames(mu_hat)[[3]]   n <- nrow(Y)   M <- dim(mu_hat)[3]   arm_idx <- match(W_char, arms)   contrast_arms <- setdiff(arms, baseline)   cn <- paste0(contrast_arms, " - ", baseline)   out <- matrix(     NA_real_,     nrow = length(contrast_arms),     ncol = M,     dimnames = list(cn, outcomes)   )   idx_row <- seq_len(n)   for (m in seq_len(M)) {     mu_w <- mu_hat[cbind(idx_row, arm_idx, m)]     for (j in seq_along(contrast_arms)) {       k <- contrast_arms[j]       mu_k <- mu_hat[, k, m]       mu_b <- mu_hat[, baseline, m]       e_k <- ps[, k]       e_b what: Doubly robust average treatment effects (AIPW plug-in)
text: non-baseline arm \(k\) outcome \(m\), use standard multi-arm doubly robust score (spirit AIPW), evaluated fitted outcome models \(\hat\mu_a(X)\) propensities \(\hat e_a(X)\): \[ \psi_i^{(k)} = \hat\mu_k(X_i) - \hat\mu_b(X_i) + \bigl(Y_{im} - \hat\mu_{W_i}(X_i)\bigr)\left(\frac{\mathbb{1}\{W_i=k\}}{\hat e_k(X_i)} - \frac{\mathbb{1}\{W_i=b\}}{\hat e_b(X_i)}\right), \] baseline \(b\) = placebo. average \(\psi_i^{(k)}\) training sample (\(Y\) observed). plug-DR estimator (nuisances fit data); rigorous inference, sample splitting cross-fitting preferred. doubly-robust estimates; ’re simply averages model’s predicted individual contrasts (use ate_log_time / ate_health_status DR averages training sample). simple check, plot contrast key covariate.
code: multi_arm_dr_ate <- function(Y, W, mu_hat, ps, baseline) {   W_char <- as.character(droplevels(W))   arms <- dimnames(mu_hat)[[2]]   outcomes <- dimnames(mu_hat)[[3]]   n <- nrow(Y)   M <- dim(mu_hat)[3]   arm_idx <- match(W_char, arms)   contrast_arms <- setdiff(arms, baseline)   cn <- paste0(contrast_arms, " - ", baseline)   out <- matrix(     NA_real_,     nrow = length(contrast_arms),     ncol = M,     dimnames = list(cn, outcomes)   )   idx_row <- seq_len(n)   for (m in seq_len(M)) {     mu_w <- mu_hat[cbind(idx_row, arm_idx, m)]     for (j in seq_along(contrast_arms)) {       k <- contrast_arms[j]       mu_k <- mu_hat[, k, m]       mu_b <- mu_hat[, baseline, m]       e_k <- ps[, k]       e_b <- ps[, baseline]       I_k <- as.numeric(W_char == k)       I_b <- as.numeric(W_char == baseline)       psi <- (mu_k - mu_b) + (Y[, m] - mu_w) * (I_k / e_k - I_b / e_b)       out[j, m] <- mean(psi)     }   }   out }  pred_train <- model$predict(X_train, drop = FALSE) ate_tab <- multi_arm_dr_ate(   Y_train,   W_train,   pred_train$mu_hat,   pred_train$propensity_score,   baseline = model$baseline ) ate_log_time <- ate_tab[, "log_time"] ate_health_status <- ate_tab[, "health_status"]  print(ate_tab) log_time health_status A - many real-world settings, treatment (like drug, policy, recommendation) doesn’t affect everyone way. Meta-learners family algorithms designed estimate much treatment affects different individuals — quantity known Conditional Average Treatment Effect (CATE): \[\tau(x) = \mathbb{E}[Y(1) - Y(0) \mid X = x]\] , \(Y(1)\) \(Y(0)\) outcomes person experience without treatment, \(X\) represents individual characteristics (covariates). Since can never observe outcomes person, need clever estimation strategies. makes meta-learners appealing flexibility: rather building specialized causal models scratch, wrap around standard machine learning model — random forests, gradient boosting, neural networks — repurpose causal estimation. Key assumption: meta-learners require unconfoundedness — condition observed covariates \(X\), treatment assignment effectively random: \[(Y(1), Y(0)) \perp T \mid X\] > causal foundation; meta-learners estimate effects vary across individuals. Idea: Train one model data, including treatment indicator \(T\) feature. \[\hat{\tau}_S(x) = \hat{\mu}(x, 1) - \hat{\mu}(x, 0)\] CATE estimated predicting outcomes treatment (\(T=1\)) control (\(T=0\)) individual, taking difference. Pros: Simple implement; naturally captures interactions treatment covariates. Cons: Tree-based models may effectively ignore \(T\) weak predictive power , leading underestimated treatment effects. Idea: Fit one model treated group another control group, subtract predictions. \[\hat{\tau}_T(x) = \hat{\mu}_1(x) - \hat{\mu}_0(x)\] Pros: Intuitive; model focuses entirely group. Cons: Struggles treatment groups imbalanced (e.g., 95% control, 5% treated) — minority-group model estimated little data high variance. Idea: extension T-Learner borrows information across groups handle imbalance. Steps: 1. Fit T-Learner models \(\hat{\mu}_0\), \(\hat{\mu}_1\) . Compute imputed treatment effects individual using opposite group’s model: treated units: \(D_i^1 = Y_i - \hat{\mu}_0(X_i)\) control units: \(D_i^0 = \hat{\mu}_1(X_i) - Y_i\) Fit models \(\hat{\tau}_1\), \(\hat{\tau}_0\) imputed effects. Combine using estimated propensity score \(g(x) = P(T=1 \mid X=x)\): \[\hat{\tau}_X(x) = g(x)\,\hat{\tau}_0(x) + (1 - g(x))\,\hat{\tau}_1(x)\] Pros: Highly efficient imbalanced treatment groups; often outperforms T-Learner empirically. Cons: Requires accurate propensity score model involves multiple fitting stages. Idea: Based Robinson’s (1988) transformation — partial effect \(X\) outcome treatment, regress residuals . Steps: Estimate nuisance functions: \(\hat{m}(x) = \mathbb{E}[Y \mid X=x]\) (expected outcome) \(\hat{e}(x) = P(T=1 \mid X=x)\) (propensity score) Compute residuals: \(\tilde{Y}_i = Y_i - \hat{m}(X_i)\) \(\tilde{T}_i = T_i - \hat{e}(X_i)\) Estimate \(\tau(x)\) solving: \[\min_{\tau} \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\tilde{Y} - \tau(X)\,\tilde{T}\right)^2\right]\] Pros: Orthogonal estimation — errors nuisance models don’t directly bias \(\hat{\tau}\). Achieves strong theoretical guarantees (Nie & Wager, 2021). Cons: complex implement; requires reasonably good nuisance estimates. Idea: Combine outcome modeling propensity scores estimator consistent either component correctly specified — necessarily . Steps: Estimate \(\hat{\mu}_0(x)\), \(\hat{\mu}_1(x)\), \(\hat{e}(x)\) one data split. Compute augmented inverse propensity weighting (AIPW) pseudo-outcomes held-data: \[\hat{\phi}_i = \underbrace{\hat{\mu}_1(X_i) - \hat{\mu}_0(X_i)}_{\text{outcome model}} + \underbrace{\frac{T_i(Y_i - \hat{\mu}_1(X_i))}{\hat{e}(X_i)} - \frac{(1-T_i)(Y_i - \hat{\mu}_0(X_i))}{1 - \hat{e}(X_i)}}_{\text{bias correction}}\] Regress \(\hat{\phi}_i\) \(X_i\) get \(\hat{\tau}_{DR}(x)\). Pros: Doubly robust — remains consistent even one misspecified component. Comes formal inference guarantees (asymptotic normality). Cons: Sensitive extreme propensity scores (near 0 1); requires careful cross-fitting. Compute imputed treatment effects individual using opposite group’s model: treated units: \(D_i^1 = Y_i - \hat{\mu}_0(X_i)\) control units: \(D_i^0 = \hat{\mu}_1(X_i) - Y_i\) Fit models \(\hat{\tau}_1\), \(\hat{\tau}_0\) imputed effects. Combine using estimated propensity score \(g(x) = P(T=1 \mid X=x)\): \[\hat{\tau}_X(x) = g(x)\,\hat{\tau}_0(x) + (1 - g(x))\,\hat{\tau}_1(x)\] Pros: Highly efficient imbalanced treatment groups; often outperforms T-Learner empirically. Cons: Requires accurate propensity score model involves multiple fitting stages.

Idea: Based Robinson’s (1988) transformation — partial effect \(X\) outcome treatment, regress residuals . Steps: Estimate nuisance functions: \(\hat{m}(x) = \mathbb{E}[Y \mid X=x]\) (expected outcome) \(\hat{e}(x) = P(T=1 \mid X=x)\) (propensity score) Compute residuals: \(\tilde{Y}_i = Y_i - \hat{m}(X_i)\) \(\tilde{T}_i = T_i - \hat{e}(X_i)\) Estimate \(\tau(x)\) solving: \[\min_{\tau} \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\tilde{Y} - \tau(X)\,\tilde{T}\right)^2\right]\] Pros: Orthogonal estimation — errors nuisance models don’t directly bias \(\hat{\tau}\). Achieves strong theoretical guarantees (Nie & Wager, 2021). Cons: complex implement; requires reasonably good nuisance estimates.

Idea: Combine outcome modeling propensity scores estimator consistent either component correctly specified — necessarily . Steps: Estimate \(\hat{\mu}_0(x)\), \(\hat{\mu}_1(x)\), \(\hat{e}(x)\) one data split. Compute augmented inverse propensity weighting (AIPW) pseudo-outcomes held-data: \[\hat{\phi}_i = \underbrace{\hat{\mu}_1(X_i) - \hat{\mu}_0(X_i)}_{\text{outcome model}} + \underbrace{\frac{T_i(Y_i - \hat{\mu}_1(X_i))}{\hat{e}(X_i)} - \frac{(1-T_i)(Y_i - \hat{\mu}_0(X_i))}{1 - \hat{e}(X_i)}}_{\text{bias correction}}\] Regress \(\hat{\phi}_i\) \(X_i\) get \(\hat{\tau}_{DR}(x)\). Pros: Doubly robust — remains consistent even one misspecified component. Comes formal inference guarantees (asymptotic normality). Cons: Sensitive extreme propensity scores (near 0 1); requires careful cross-fitting.

Distribution of CATE predictions by meta learner (T, X, R with LR, RF, XGB) alpha <- 0.2 bins <- 30 par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1)) hist(cate_t_lr, col = adjustcolor("blue", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA,      main = "Distribution of CATE Predictions by Meta Learner",      xlab = "Individual Treatment Effect (ITE/CATE)", ylab = "# of Samples") hist(cate_t_rf, col = adjustcolor("cyan", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA, add = TRUE) hist(cate_t_xgb, col = adjustcolor("navy", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA, add = TRUE) hist(cate_x_lr, col = adjustcolor("red", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA, add = TRUE) hist(cate_x_rf, col = adjustcolor("orange", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA, add = TRUE) hist(cate_x_xgb, col = adjustcolor("darkred", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA, add = TRUE) hist(cate_r_lr, col = adjustcolor("green", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA, add = TRUE) hist(cate_r_rf, col = adjustcolor("darkgreen", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA, add = TRUE) hist(cate_r_xgb, col = adjustcolor("forestgreen", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA, add = TRUE) s_val <- if (length(cate_s) > 1) mean(cate_s) else cate_s[1] abline(v = s_val, lty = 2, col = "black", lwd = 2) legend("topright",        legend = c("T (LR)", "T (RF)", "T (XGB)", "X (LR)", "X (RF)", "X (XGB)", "R (LR)", "R (RF)", "R (XGB)", "S Learner"),        fill = c("blue", "cyan", "navy", "red", "orange", "darkred", "green", "darkgreen", "forestgreen", NA),        lty = c(rep(NA, 9), 2), lwd = c(rep(NA, 9), 2), col = c(rep(NA, 9), "black"), border = NA, cex = 0.7)

Mirror Python get_synthetic_preds_holdout(simulate_nuisance_and_easy_treatment, n=50000, valid_size=0.2).     Area cumulative gain curve (Qini score package).
code: # Validate meta-learners: Linear Regression (LR), Random Forest (ranger), XGBoost (XGB) # k runs, train/validation split; report Abs % Error ATE, MSE, KL Divergence k <- k_holdout n_sim <- n_sim_holdout valid_frac <- 0.2 learners_lab <- c(   "S Learner (LR)", "S Learner (RF)", "S Learner (XGB)",   "T Learner (LR)", "T Learner (RF)", "T Learner (XGB)",   "X Learner (LR)", "X Learner (RF)", "X Learner (XGB)",   "R Learner (LR)", "R Learner (RF)", "R Learner (XGB)" ) n_learners <- length(learners_lab) train_abs_ate <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) train_mse <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) train_kl <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) valid_abs_ate <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) valid_mse <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) valid_kl <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) kl_div <- function(tau, pred, n_bins = 20) {   br <- seq(min(tau, pred, na.rm = TRUE), max(tau, pred, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = n_bins + 1)   p_act <- table(cut(tau, br, include.lowest = TRUE)) / length(tau)   p_pred <- table(cut(pred, br, include.lowest = TRUE)) / length(pred)   p_pred <- p_pred + 1e-10   p_act <- p_act + 1e-10   p_act <- p_act / sum(p_act)   p_pred <- p_pred / sum(p_pred)   sum(p_act * (log(p_act) - log(p_pred))) } for (run in seq_len(k)) {   d_run <- simulate_nuisance_and_easy_treatment(n = n_sim, p = 8, sigma = 1)   n_valid <- round(n_sim * valid_frac)   idx_valid <- seq_len(n_valid)   idx_train <- seq(n_valid + 1, n_sim)   X_tr <- d_run$X[idx_train, , drop = FALSE]   X_va <- d_run$X[idx_valid, , drop = FALSE]   w_tr <- d_run$w[idx_train]   y_tr <- d_run$y[idx_train]   e_tr <- d_run$e[idx_train]   tau_tr <- d_run$tau[idx_train]   tau_va <- d_run$tau[idx_valid]   true_ate <- mean(tau_va)   # Fit all learners: LR, RF (ranger), XGB for S, T, X, R (lighter options when fast_run)   l_s_lr <- fit(LRSRegressor(), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr)   l_s_rf <- fit(SLearner(learner = "ranger"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, num.trees = num_trees_rf)   l_s_xgb <- fit(SLearner(learner = "xgb"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, nrounds = nrounds_xgb)   l_t_lr <- fit(TLearner(learner = "lm"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr)   l_t_rf <- fit(TLearner(learner = "ranger"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, num.trees = num_trees_rf)   l_t_xgb <- fit(TLearner(learner = "xgb"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, nrounds = nrounds_xgb)   l_x_lr <- fit(XLearner(learner = "lm"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr)   l_x_rf <- fit(XLearner(learner = "ranger"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr, num.trees = num_trees_rf)   l_x_xgb <- fit(XLearner(learner = "xgb"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr, nrounds = nrounds_xgb)   l_r_lr <- fit(RLearner(learner = "lm", n_fold = n_fold_r), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr)   l_r_rf <- fit(RLearner(learner = "ranger", n_fold = n_fold_r), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr, num.trees = num_trees_rf)   l_r_xgb <- fit(RLearner(learner = "xgb", n_fold = n_fold_r), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr, nrounds = nrounds_xgb)   preds_tr <- list(     predict(l_s_lr, X_tr), predict(l_s_rf, X_tr), predict(l_s_xgb, X_tr),     predict(l_t_lr, X_tr), predict(l_t_rf, X_tr), predict(l_t_xgb, X_tr),     predict(l_x_lr, X_tr), predict(l_x_rf, X_tr), predict(l_x_xgb, X_tr),     predict(l_r_lr, X_tr), predict(l_r_rf, X_tr), predict(l_r_xgb, X_tr)   )   preds_va <- list(     predict(l_s_lr, X_va), predict(l_s_rf, X_va), predict(l_s_xgb, X_va),     predict(l_t_lr, X_va), predict(l_t_rf, X_va), predict(l_t_xgb, X_va),     predict(l_x_lr, X_va), predict(l_x_rf, X_va), predict(l_x_xgb, X_va),     predict(l_r_lr, X_va), predict(l_r_rf, X_va), predict(l_r_xgb, X_va)   )   for (j in seq_len(n_learners)) {     all_na_tr <- all(is.na(preds_tr[[j]]))     all_na_va <- all(is.na(preds_va[[j]]))     if (all_na_tr) {       train_abs_ate[run, j] <- NA_real_       train_mse[run, j] <- NA_real_       train_kl[run, j] <- NA_real_     } else {       ate_j_tr <- mean(preds_tr[[j]], na.rm = TRUE)       train_abs_ate[run, j] <- abs(ate_j_tr - mean(tau_tr)) / max(abs(mean(tau_tr)), 1e-10)       train_mse[run, j] <- mean((preds_tr[[j]] - tau_tr)^2, na.rm = TRUE)       train_kl[run, j] <- tryCatch(kl_div(tau_tr, preds_tr[[j]]), error = function(e) NA_real_)     }     if (all_na_va) {       valid_abs_ate[run, j] <- NA_real_       valid_mse[run, j] <- NA_real_       valid_kl[run, j] <- NA_real_     } else {       ate_j_va <- mean(preds_va[[j]], na.rm = TRUE)       valid_abs_ate[run, j] <- abs(ate_j_va - true_ate) / max(abs(true_ate), 1e-10)       valid_mse[run, j] <- mean((preds_va[[j]] - tau_va)^2, na.rm = TRUE)       valid_kl[run, j] <- tryCatch(kl_div(tau_va, preds_va[[j]]), error = function(e) NA_real_)     }   } } cm_tr_ate <- colMeans(train_abs_ate, na.rm = TRUE) cm_tr_mse <- colMeans(train_mse, na.rm = TRUE) cm_tr_kl <- colMeans(train_kl, na.rm = TRUE) cm_va_ate <- colMeans(valid_abs_ate, na.rm = TRUE) cm_va_mse <- colMeans(valid_mse, na.rm = TRUE) cm_va_kl <- colMeans(valid_kl, na.rm = TRUE) cm_tr_ate[is.nan(cm_tr_ate)] <- NA cm_tr_mse[is.nan(cm_tr_mse)] <- NA cm_tr_kl[is.nan(cm_tr_kl)] <- NA cm_va_ate[is.nan(cm_va_ate)] <- NA cm_va_mse[is.nan(cm_va_mse)] <- NA cm_va_kl[is.nan(cm_va_kl)] <- NA train_summary <- data.frame(   Learner = c("Actuals", learners_lab),   Abs_Pct_Error_ATE = c(0, cm_tr_ate),   MSE = c(0, cm_tr_mse),   KL_Divergence = c(0, cm_tr_kl) ) validation_summary <- data.frame(   Learner = c("Actuals", learners_lab),   Abs_Pct_Error_ATE = c(0, cm_va_ate),   MSE = c(0, cm_va_mse),   KL_Divergence = c(0, cm_va_kl) ) train_display <- train_summary for (col in c("Abs_Pct_Error_ATE", "MSE", "KL_Divergence")) {   train_display[[col]] <- ifelse(is.na(train_summary[[col]]), "—",     format(round(train_summary[[col]], 6), nsmall = 6)) } knitr::kable(train_display, col.names = c("", "Abs % Error of ATE", "MSE", "KL Divergence")) valid_display <- validation_summary for (col in c("Abs_Pct_Error_ATE", "MSE", "KL_Divergence")) {   valid_display[[col]] <- ifelse(is.na(validation_summary[[col]]), "—",     format(round(validation_summary[[col]], 6), nsmall = 6)) } knitr::kable(valid_display, col.names = c("", "Abs % Error of ATE", "MSE", "KL Divergence")) # One panel per metric: x = train, y = validation (one point per learner, excluding Actuals) par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) tr <- train_summary[-1, ] va <- validation_summary[-1, ] ok <- is.finite(tr$Abs_Pct_Error_ATE) & is.finite(va$Abs_Pct_Error_ATE) tr <- tr[ok, ]; va <- va[ok, ] if (nrow(tr) > 0) { plot(tr$Abs_Pct_Error_ATE, va$Abs_Pct_Error_ATE, pch = 19, xlab = "Train", ylab = "Validation",      main = "Abs % Error of ATE") text(tr$Abs_Pct_Error_ATE, va$Abs_Pct_Error_ATE, tr$Learner, pos = 4, cex = 0.7) abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "gray") plot(tr$MSE, va$MSE, pch = 19, xlab = "Train", ylab = "Validation", main = "MSE") text(tr$MSE, va$MSE, tr$Learner, pos = 4, cex = 0.7) abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "gray") plot(tr$KL_Divergence, va$KL_Divergence, pch = 19, xlab = "Train", ylab = "Validation", main = "KL Divergence") text(tr$KL_Divergence, va$KL_Divergence, tr$Learner, pos = 4, cex = 0.7) abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "gray") } par(mfrow = c(1, 1)) drop_learners <- "S Learner (LR)"  # S-learner is constant CATE; drop to compare T/X/R tr2 <- tr[!tr$Learner %in% drop_learners, ] va2 <- va[!va$Learner %in% drop_learners, ] tr2 <- tr2[is.finite(tr2$Abs_Pct_Error_ATE), ] va2 <- main = "Train: Abs % Error of ATE", ylab = "Abs % Error of ATE")   barplot(tr2$MSE, names.arg = tr2$Learner, las = 2, col = "darkorange",           main = "Train: MSE", ylab = "MSE")   barplot(tr2$KL_Divergence, names.arg = tr2$Learner, las = 2, col = "forestgreen",           main = "Train: KL Divergence", ylab = "KL Divergence")   par(mfrow = c(1, 1)) } if (nrow(va2) > 0) { par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(8, 4, 2, 1)) barplot(va2$Abs_Pct_Error_ATE, names.arg = va2$Learner, las = 2, col = "steelblue",         main = "Validation: Abs % Error of ATE", ylab = "Abs % Error of ATE") barplot(va2$MSE, names.arg = va2$Learner, las = 2, col = "darkorange",         main = "Validation: MSE", ylab = "MSE") barplot(va2$KL_Divergence, names.arg = va2$Learner, las = 2, col = "forestgreen",         main = "Validation: KL Divergence", ylab = "KL Divergence") par(mfrow = c(1, 1)) } # Single run: validate Linear Regression, Random Forest (ranger), XGBoost n_one <- n_one_pred set.seed(101) d_one <- simulate_nuisance_and_easy_treatment(n = n_one, p = 8, sigma = 1) n_valid_one <- round(n_one * 0.2) idx_va_one <- seq_len(n_valid_one) idx_tr_one <- seq(n_valid_one + 1, n_one) X_tr_one <- d_one$X[idx_tr_one, , drop = FALSE] X_va_one <- d_one$X[idx_va_one, , drop = FALSE] w_tr_one <- d_one$w[idx_tr_one] y_tr_one <- d_one$y[idx_tr_one] e_tr_one <- d_one$e[idx_tr_one] X_tr_one, w_tr_one, y_tr_one) ls_s_rf <- fit(SLearner(learner = "ranger"), X_tr_one, w_tr_one, y_tr_one, num.trees = num_trees_rf) ls_s_xgb <- fit(SLearner(learner = "xgb"), X_tr_one, w_tr_one, num_trees_rf) ls_t_xgb <- fit(TLearner(learner = "xgb"), X_tr_one, w_tr_one, y_tr_one, nrounds = nrounds_xgb) ls_x_lr <- fit(XLearner(learner = "lm"), X_tr_one, w_tr_one, y_tr_one, p = e_tr_one) e_tr_one, nrounds = nrounds_xgb) ls_r_lr <- fit(RLearner(learner = "lm", n_fold = n_fold_r), X_tr_one, w_tr_one, y_tr_one, p = e_tr_one) ls_r_rf <- fit(RLearner(learner = "ranger", n_fold = n_fold_r), X_tr_one, w_tr_one, y_tr_one, p = e_tr_one, num.trees = num_trees_rf) ls_r_xgb <- fit(RLearner(learner = "xgb", n_fold = n_fold_r), X_tr_one, w_tr_one, y_tr_one, p = e_tr_one, nrounds = nrounds_xgb) xr, ylim = yr)   abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "red") } par(mfrow = c(1, 1)) # AUUC = area under cumulative gain (same as qini_curve then trapezoidal sum) # Inline to avoid depending on package export auuc_vec <- function(tau, pred) {   n <- length(tau)   if (n < 2) return(0)   ord <- order(pred, decreasing = TRUE)   qc <- cumsum(tau[ord])   sum((qc[-1] + qc[-n]) / 2) } qini_curve_local <- what: Holdout summary (k runs; reduced when fast_run)
code: # Validate meta-learners: Linear Regression (LR), Random Forest (ranger), XGBoost (XGB) # k runs, train/validation split; report Abs % Error ATE, MSE, KL Divergence k <- k_holdout n_sim <- n_sim_holdout valid_frac <- 0.2 learners_lab <- c(   "S Learner (LR)", "S Learner (RF)", "S Learner (XGB)",   "T Learner (LR)", "T Learner (RF)", "T Learner (XGB)",   "X Learner (LR)", "X Learner (RF)", "X Learner (XGB)",   "R Learner (LR)", "R Learner (RF)", "R Learner (XGB)" ) n_learners <- length(learners_lab) train_abs_ate <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) train_mse <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) train_kl <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) valid_abs_ate <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) valid_mse <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) valid_kl <- matrix(NA_real_, k, n_learners) kl_div <- function(tau, pred, n_bins = 20) {   br <- seq(min(tau, pred, na.rm = TRUE), max(tau, pred, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = n_bins + 1)   p_act <- table(cut(tau, br, include.lowest = TRUE)) / length(tau)   p_pred <- table(cut(pred, br, include.lowest = TRUE)) / length(pred)   p_pred <- p_pred + 1e-10   p_act <- p_act + 1e-10   p_act <- p_act / sum(p_act)   p_pred <- p_pred / sum(p_pred)   sum(p_act * (log(p_act) - log(p_pred))) } for (run in seq_len(k)) {   d_run <- simulate_nuisance_and_easy_treatment(n = n_sim, p = 8, sigma = 1)   n_valid <- round(n_sim * valid_frac)   idx_valid <- seq_len(n_valid)   idx_train <- seq(n_valid + 1, n_sim)   X_tr <- d_run$X[idx_train, , drop = FALSE]   X_va <- d_run$X[idx_valid, , drop = FALSE]   w_tr <- d_run$w[idx_train]   y_tr <- d_run$y[idx_train]   e_tr <- d_run$e[idx_train]   tau_tr <- d_run$tau[idx_train]   tau_va <- d_run$tau[idx_valid]   true_ate <- mean(tau_va)   # Fit all learners: LR, RF (ranger), XGB for S, T, X, R (lighter options when fast_run)   l_s_lr <- fit(LRSRegressor(), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr)   l_s_rf <- fit(SLearner(learner = "ranger"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, num.trees = num_trees_rf)   l_s_xgb <- fit(SLearner(learner = "xgb"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, nrounds = nrounds_xgb)   l_t_lr <- fit(TLearner(learner = "lm"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr)   l_t_rf <- fit(TLearner(learner = "ranger"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, num.trees = num_trees_rf)   l_t_xgb <- fit(TLearner(learner = "xgb"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, nrounds = nrounds_xgb)   l_x_lr <- fit(XLearner(learner = "lm"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr)   l_x_rf <- fit(XLearner(learner = "ranger"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr, num.trees = num_trees_rf)   l_x_xgb <- fit(XLearner(learner = "xgb"), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr, nrounds = nrounds_xgb)   l_r_lr <- fit(RLearner(learner = "lm", n_fold = n_fold_r), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr)   l_r_rf <- fit(RLearner(learner = "ranger", n_fold = n_fold_r), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr, num.trees = num_trees_rf)   l_r_xgb <- fit(RLearner(learner = "xgb", n_fold = n_fold_r), X_tr, w_tr, y_tr, p = e_tr, nrounds = nrounds_xgb)   preds_tr <- list(     predict(l_s_lr, X_tr), predict(l_s_rf, X_tr), predict(l_s_xgb, X_tr),     predict(l_t_lr, X_tr), predict(l_t_rf, X_tr), predict(l_t_xgb, X_tr),     predict(l_x_lr, X_tr), predict(l_x_rf, X_tr), predict(l_x_xgb, X_tr),     predict(l_r_lr, X_tr), predict(l_r_rf, X_tr), predict(l_r_xgb, X_tr)   )   preds_va <- list(     predict(l_s_lr, X_va), predict(l_s_rf, X_va), predict(l_s_xgb, X_va),     predict(l_t_lr, X_va), predict(l_t_rf, X_va), predict(l_t_xgb, X_va),     predict(l_x_lr, X_va), predict(l_x_rf, X_va), predict(l_x_xgb, X_va),     predict(l_r_lr, X_va), predict(l_r_rf, X_va), predict(l_r_xgb, X_va)   )   for (j in seq_len(n_learners)) {     all_na_tr <- all(is.na(preds_tr[[j]]))     all_na_va <- all(is.na(preds_va[[j]]))     if (all_na_tr) {       train_abs_ate[run, j] <- NA_real_       train_mse[run, j] <- NA_real_       train_kl[run, j] <- NA_real_     } else {       ate_j_tr <- mean(preds_tr[[j]], na.rm = TRUE)       train_abs_ate[run, j] <- abs(ate_j_tr - mean(tau_tr)) / max(abs(mean(tau_tr)), 1e-10)       train_mse[run, j] <- mean((preds_tr[[j]] - tau_tr)^2, na.rm = TRUE)       train_kl[run, j] <- tryCatch(kl_div(tau_tr, preds_tr[[j]]), error = function(e) NA_real_)     }     if (all_na_va) {       valid_abs_ate[run, j] <- NA_real_       valid_mse[run, j] <- NA_real_       valid_kl[run, j] <- NA_real_     } else {       ate_j_va <- mean(preds_va[[j]], na.rm = TRUE)       valid_abs_ate[run, j] <- abs(ate_j_va - true_ate) / max(abs(true_ate), 1e-10)       valid_mse[run, j] <- mean((preds_va[[j]] - tau_va)^2, na.rm = TRUE)       valid_kl[run, j] <- tryCatch(kl_div(tau_va, preds_va[[j]]), error = function(e) NA_real_)     }   } } cm_tr_ate <- colMeans(train_abs_ate, na.rm = TRUE) cm_tr_mse <- colMeans(train_mse, na.rm = TRUE) cm_tr_kl <- colMeans(train_kl, na.rm = TRUE) cm_va_ate <- colMeans(valid_abs_ate, na.rm = TRUE) cm_va_mse <- colMeans(valid_mse, na.rm = TRUE) cm_va_kl <- colMeans(valid_kl, na.rm = TRUE) cm_tr_ate[is.nan(cm_tr_ate)] <- NA cm_tr_mse[is.nan(cm_tr_mse)] <- NA cm_tr_kl[is.nan(cm_tr_kl)] <- NA cm_va_ate[is.nan(cm_va_ate)] <- NA cm_va_mse[is.nan(cm_va_mse)] <- NA cm_va_kl[is.nan(cm_va_kl)] <- NA train_summary <- data.frame(   Learner = c("Actuals", learners_lab),   Abs_Pct_Error_ATE = c(0, cm_tr_ate),   MSE = c(0, cm_tr_mse),   KL_Divergence = c(0, cm_tr_kl) ) validation_summary <- data.frame(   Learner = c("Actuals", learners_lab),   Abs_Pct_Error_ATE = c(0, cm_va_ate),   MSE = c(0, cm_va_mse),   KL_Divergence = c(0, cm_va_kl) )

train_display <- train_summary for (col in c("Abs_Pct_Error_ATE", "MSE", "KL_Divergence")) {   train_display[[col]] <- ifelse(is.na(train_summary[[col]]), "—",     format(round(train_summary[[col]], 6), nsmall = 6)) } knitr::kable(train_display, col.names = c("", "Abs % Error of ATE", "MSE", "KL Divergence"))

valid_display <- validation_summary for (col in c("Abs_Pct_Error_ATE", "MSE", "KL_Divergence")) {   valid_display[[col]] <- ifelse(is.na(validation_summary[[col]]), "—",     format(round(validation_summary[[col]], 6), nsmall = 6)) } knitr::kable(valid_display, col.names = c("", "Abs % Error of ATE", "MSE", "KL Divergence"))

text: Area cumulative gain curve (Qini score package).
code: # AUUC = area under cumulative gain (same as qini_curve then trapezoidal sum) # Inline to avoid depending on package export auuc_vec <- function(tau, pred) {   n <- length(tau)   if (n < 2) return(0)   ord <- order(pred, decreasing = TRUE)   qc <- cumsum(tau[ord])   sum((qc[-1] + qc[-n]) / 2) } qini_curve_local <- function(tau, pred) {   ord <- order(pred, decreasing = TRUE)   cumsum(tau[ord]) } # Table: cum_gain_auuc for each learner + Actuals + Random train_auuc <- data.frame(   Learner = c("Actuals", setdiff(names(train_preds), "Actuals"), "Random"),   cum_gain_auuc = c(     auuc_vec(train_preds$Actuals, train_preds$Actuals),     sapply(setdiff(names(train_preds), "Actuals"), function(col) auuc_vec(train_preds$Actuals, train_preds[[col]])),     auuc_vec(train_preds$Actuals, runif(nrow(train_preds)))   ) ) train_auuc <- train_auuc[order(-train_auuc$cum_gain_auuc), ] knitr::kable(train_auuc, digits = 6, row.names = FALSE) # Cumulative gain curves — Training (drop S-learners for readability) model_cols_auuc <- setdiff(names(train_preds), c("Actuals", "S_Learner_LR", "S_Learner_RF", "S_Learner_XGB")) tau_tr <- train_preds$Actuals n_tr <- length(tau_tr) frac <- (1:n_tr) / n_tr par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, max(qini_curve_local(tau_tr, tau_tr))), type = "n",      xlab = "Population", ylab = "Cumulative gain", main = "Cumulative Gain (Training)") cols <- seq_along(model_cols_auuc) for (i in seq_along(model_cols_auuc)) {   qc <- qini_curve_local(tau_tr, train_preds[[model_cols_auuc[i]]])   lines(frac, qc, col = cols[i], lwd = 2) } legend("bottomright", legend = model_cols_auuc, col = cols, lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.7) valid_auuc <- data.frame(   Learner = c("Actuals", setdiff(names(valid_preds), "Actuals"), "Random"),   cum_gain_auuc = c(     auuc_vec(valid_preds$Actuals, valid_preds$Actuals),     sapply(setdiff(names(valid_preds), "Actuals"), function(col) auuc_vec(valid_preds$Actuals, valid_preds[[col]])),     auuc_vec(valid_preds$Actuals, runif(nrow(valid_preds)))   ) ) valid_auuc <- valid_auuc[order(-valid_auuc$cum_gain_auuc), ] knitr::kable(valid_auuc, digits = 6, row.names = FALSE) tau_va <- valid_preds$Actuals n_va <- length(tau_va) frac_va <- (1:n_va) / n_va plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, max(qini_curve_local(tau_va, tau_va))), type = "n",      xlab = "Population", ylab = "Cumulative gain", main = "Cumulative Gain (Validation)") for (i in seq_along(model_cols_auuc)) {   if (model_cols_auuc[i] %in% names(valid_preds)) {     qc <- qini_curve_local(tau_va, valid_preds[[model_cols_auuc[i]]])     lines(frac_va, qc, col = cols[i], lwd = 2)   } } legend("bottomright", legend = model_cols_auuc, col = cols, lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.7)

what: Part A: Synthetic data, problem formulation, X- and DR-learners
text: simulate \(K=3\) arms multinomial assignment, known \(\tau_1(x)\), \(\tau_2(x)\) versus control, store true propensities diagnostics. \(K\) arms (\(T \\{0,1,\dots,K-1\}\)), estimate \(K-1\) CATE functions relative control (\(T=0\)): \[\tau_k(x) = \mathbb{E}[Y(k) - Y(0) \mid X = x], \quad k = 1,\dots,K-1\] Challenges include multinomial propensities \(e_k(x) = P(T=k \mid X=x)\), sparse arms, careful cross-fitting split data (illustrated Part B). extend X-learner using outcome models per arm, imputed treatment effects, propensity-based weights, CATE regression per non-control arm (ranger via mlr3). Doubly robust scores use estimated multinomial propensities outcome models per arm; regress score \(X\) contrast vs. control. Figure 1
code:
generate_multi_treatment_data <- function(n = 6000, K = 3) {   X <- matrix(rnorm(n * 10), nrow = n)   colnames(X) <- paste0("X", 1:10)   eta <- cbind(     rep(0, n),     -0.3 + 0.7 * X[, 1] - 0.5 * X[, 2],     0.2 - 0.4 * X[, 1] + 0.6 * X[, 3]   )   exp_eta <- exp(eta)   probs <- exp_eta / rowSums(exp_eta)   Tdraw <- apply(probs, 1, function(p) which(rmultinom(1, 1, p) == 1) - 1)   tau_1 <- 1.8 + 2.2 * X[, 1] - 1.0 * X[, 2]   tau_2 <- 0.5 - 1.5 * X[, 1] + 1.8 * X[, 6]   mu_0 <- 2 * X[, 1] - 1.5 * X[, 2] + X[, 4]^2 + sin(X[, 5])   Y <- mu_0 + (Tdraw == 1) * tau_1 + (Tdraw == 2) * tau_2 + rnorm(n, sd = 1.8)   df <- data.frame(Y, T = as.factor(Tdraw), as.data.frame(X))   df$tau_1_true <- tau_1   df$tau_2_true <- tau_2   df$propensity_0 <- probs[, 1]   df$propensity_1 <- probs[, 2]   df$propensity_2 <- probs[, 3]   df } df_multi <- generate_multi_treatment_data(n_multi, K = 3) covs <- paste0("X", 1:10) prop_col_multi <- function(df, arm, control_arm = "0") {   k <- as.character(arm)   if (paste0("propensity_", k) %in% names(df)) {     return(df[[paste0("propensity_", k)]])   }   stop("Data must contain propensity_", k, " for X-learner weights.") }  x_learner_multi <- function(df, outcome = "Y", treatment = "T",                             covariates = covs,                             control_arm = "0",                             n_trees_mu = n_trees_mu_x,                             n_trees_tau = n_trees_tau_x,                             newdata = NULL) {   arms <- levels(df[[treatment]])   non_control <- setdiff(arms, control_arm)   pred_rows <- if (is.null(newdata)) df else newdata    mu_models <- list()   for (arm in arms) {     df_arm <- df[df[[treatment]] == arm, , drop = FALSE]     if (nrow(df_arm) < 50) next     task <- TaskRegr$new(       id = paste0("arm_", arm),       backend = df_arm[, c(outcome, covariates)],       target = outcome     )     learner <- lrn("regr.ranger", num.trees = n_trees_mu)     learner$train(task)     mu_models[[arm]] <- learner   }    tau_models <- list()   tau_estimates <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(pred_rows), ncol = length(non_control))   colnames(tau_estimates) <- paste0("tau_", non_control)    p0 <- prop_col_multi(df, control_arm, control_arm)    for (idx in seq_along(non_control)) {     arm <- non_control[idx]     pk <- prop_col_multi(df, arm, control_arm)     mu_0_fit <- mu_models[[control_arm]]$predict_newdata(df[, covariates])$response     mu_k_fit <- mu_models[[arm]]$predict_newdata(df[, covariates])$response     D_imputed <- ifelse(df[[treatment]] == control_arm,       mu_k_fit - df[[outcome]],       df[[outcome]] - mu_0_fit     )     weights <- ifelse(df[[treatment]] == control_arm, pk / p0, 1.0)     df_tau <- data.frame(tau = D_imputed, weight = weights, df[, covariates])     task_tau <- TaskRegr$new(       id = paste0("tau_", arm),       backend = df_tau,       target = "tau"     )     task_tau$set_col_roles("weight", roles = "weights_learner")     learner_tau <- lrn("regr.ranger", num.trees = n_trees_tau)     learner_tau$train(task_tau)     tau_models[[arm]] <- learner_tau     tau_estimates[, idx] <- learner_tau$predict_newdata(pred_rows[, covariates])$response   }    res <- as.data.frame(tau_estimates)   if ("tau_1_true" %in% names(pred_rows)) res$tau_1_true <- pred_rows$tau_1_true   if ("tau_2_true" %in% names(pred_rows)) res$tau_2_true <- pred_rows$tau_2_true   res }  x_multi_res <- x_learner_multi(df_multi) rmse_arm1 <- sqrt(mean((x_multi_res$tau_1 - x_multi_res$tau_1_true)^2)) rmse_arm2 <- sqrt(mean((x_multi_res$tau_2 - x_multi_res$tau_2_true)^2)) cat("Multi-arm X-Learner RMSE (full sample):
") Multi-arm X-Learner RMSE (full sample): cat("  Arm 1 vs control:", round(rmse_arm1, 3), "
") Arm 1 vs control: 2.408 cat("  Arm 2 vs control:", round(rmse_arm2, 3), "
") Arm 2 vs control: 3.034 dr_learner_multi <- function(df, outcome = "Y", treatment = "T",                              covariates = covs,                              control_arm = "0",                              n_trees_mu = n_trees_mu_dr,                              n_trees_score = n_trees_score_dr,                              newdata = NULL) {   arms <- levels(df[[treatment]])   non_control <- setdiff(arms, control_arm)   pred_rows <- if (is.null(newdata)) df else newdata    prop_model <- multinom(     as.formula(paste(treatment, "~", paste(covariates, collapse = "+"))),     data = df,     trace = FALSE   )   prop_preds <- predict(prop_model, df[, covariates], type = "probs")   cn <- colnames(prop_preds)   if (is.null(cn)) {     lev <- levels(df[[treatment]])     colnames(prop_preds) <- lev     cn <- lev   }    idx_e <- function(arm) {     j <- match(as.character(arm), cn)     if (is.na(j)) stop("Propensity column not found for arm ", arm)     j   }    mu_models <- list()   for (arm in arms) {     df_arm <- df[df[[treatment]] == arm, , drop = FALSE]     task <- TaskRegr$new(       id = paste0("arm_", arm),       backend = df_arm[, c(outcome, covariates)],       target = outcome     )     learner <- lrn("regr.ranger", num.trees = n_trees_mu)     learner$train(task)     mu_models[[arm]] <- learner   }    dr_estimates <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(pred_rows), ncol = length(non_control))   colnames(dr_estimates) <- paste0("tau_dr_", non_control)    j0 <- idx_e(control_arm)    for (idx in seq_along(non_control)) {     arm <- non_control[idx]     jk <- idx_e(arm)     mu_0_hat <- mu_models[[control_arm]]$predict_newdata(df[, covariates])$response     mu_k_hat <- mu_models[[arm]]$predict_newdata(df[, covariates])$response     e0 <- prop_preds[, j0]     ek <- prop_preds[, jk]     score <- ifelse(df[[treatment]] == arm,       (df[[outcome]] - mu_k_hat) / ek, 0     ) - ifelse(df[[treatment]] == control_arm,       (df[[outcome]] - mu_0_hat) / e0, 0     ) + mu_k_hat - mu_0_hat     df_score <- data.frame(score = score, df[, covariates])     task_score <- TaskRegr$new(       id = paste0("dr_", arm),       backend = df_score,       target = "score"     )     learner_score <- lrn("regr.ranger", num.trees = n_trees_score)     learner_score$train(task_score)     dr_estimates[, idx] <- learner_score$predict_newdata(pred_rows[, covariates])$response   }    res <- as.data.frame(dr_estimates)   if ("tau_1_true" %in% names(pred_rows)) res$tau_1_true <- pred_rows$tau_1_true   if ("tau_2_true" %in% names(pred_rows)) res$tau_2_true <- pred_rows$tau_2_true   res }  dr_multi_res <- dr_learner_multi(df_multi) rmse_dr1 <- sqrt(mean((dr_multi_res$tau_dr_1 - dr_multi_res$tau_1_true)^2)) rmse_dr2 <- sqrt(mean((dr_multi_res$tau_dr_2 - dr_multi_res$tau_2_true)^2)) cat("DR-Learner RMSE (full sample):

code: generate_multi_treatment_data <- function(n = 6000, K = 3) {   X <- matrix(rnorm(n * 10), nrow = n)   colnames(X) <- paste0("X", 1:10)   eta <- cbind(     rep(0, n),     -0.3 + 0.7 * X[, 1] - 0.5 * X[, 2],     0.2 - 0.4 * X[, 1] + 0.6 * X[, 3]   )   exp_eta <- exp(eta)   probs <- exp_eta / rowSums(exp_eta)   Tdraw <- apply(probs, 1, function(p) which(rmultinom(1, 1, p) == 1) - 1)   tau_1 <- 1.8 + 2.2 * X[, 1] - 1.0 * X[, 2]   tau_2 <- 0.5 - 1.5 * X[, 1] + 1.8 * X[, 6]   mu_0 <- 2 * X[, 1] - 1.5 * X[, 2] + X[, 4]^2 + sin(X[, 5])   Y <- mu_0 + (Tdraw == 1) * tau_1 + (Tdraw == 2) * tau_2 + rnorm(n, sd = 1.8)   df <- data.frame(Y, T = as.factor(Tdraw), as.data.frame(X))   df$tau_1_true <- tau_1   df$tau_2_true <- tau_2   df$propensity_0 <- probs[, 1]   df$propensity_1 <- probs[, 2]   df$propensity_2 <- probs[, 3]   df } df_multi <- generate_multi_treatment_data(n_multi, K = 3) covs <- paste0("X", 1:10)

dr_learner_multi <- function(df, outcome = "Y", treatment = "T",                              covariates = covs,                              control_arm = "0",                              n_trees_mu = n_trees_mu_dr,                              n_trees_score = n_trees_score_dr,                              newdata = NULL) {   arms <- levels(df[[treatment]])   non_control <- setdiff(arms, control_arm)   pred_rows <- if (is.null(newdata)) df else newdata    prop_model <- multinom(     as.formula(paste(treatment, "~", paste(covariates, collapse = "+"))),     data = df,     trace = FALSE   )   prop_preds <- predict(prop_model, df[, covariates], type = "probs")   cn <- colnames(prop_preds)   if (is.null(cn)) {     lev <- levels(df[[treatment]])     colnames(prop_preds) <- lev     cn <- lev   }    idx_e <- function(arm) {     j <- match(as.character(arm), cn)     if (is.na(j)) stop("Propensity column not found for arm ", arm)     j   }    mu_models <- list()   for (arm in arms) {     df_arm <- df[df[[treatment]] == arm, , drop = FALSE]     task <- TaskRegr$new(       id = paste0("arm_", arm),       backend = df_arm[, c(outcome, covariates)],       target = outcome     )     learner <- lrn("regr.ranger", num.trees = n_trees_mu)     learner$train(task)     mu_models[[arm]] <- learner   }    dr_estimates <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(pred_rows), ncol = length(non_control))   colnames(dr_estimates) <- paste0("tau_dr_", non_control)    j0 <- idx_e(control_arm)    for (idx in seq_along(non_control)) {     arm <- non_control[idx]     jk <- idx_e(arm)     mu_0_hat <- mu_models[[control_arm]]$predict_newdata(df[, covariates])$response     mu_k_hat <- mu_models[[arm]]$predict_newdata(df[, covariates])$response     e0 <- prop_preds[, j0]     ek <- prop_preds[, jk]     score <- ifelse(df[[treatment]] == arm,       (df[[outcome]] - mu_k_hat) / ek, 0     ) - ifelse(df[[treatment]] == control_arm,       (df[[outcome]] - mu_0_hat) / e0, 0     ) + mu_k_hat - mu_0_hat     df_score <- data.frame(score = score, df[, covariates])     task_score <- TaskRegr$new(       id = paste0("dr_", arm),       backend = df_score,       target = "score"     )     learner_score <- lrn("regr.ranger", num.trees = n_trees_score)     learner_score$train(task_score)     dr_estimates[, idx] <- learner_score$predict_newdata(pred_rows[, covariates])$response   }    res <- as.data.frame(dr_estimates)   if ("tau_1_true" %in% names(pred_rows)) res$tau_1_true <- pred_rows$tau_1_true   if ("tau_2_true" %in% names(pred_rows)) res$tau_2_true <- pred_rows$tau_2_true   res }  dr_multi_res <- dr_learner_multi(df_multi) rmse_dr1 <- sqrt(mean((dr_multi_res$tau_dr_1 - dr_multi_res$tau_1_true)^2)) rmse_dr2 <- sqrt(mean((dr_multi_res$tau_dr_2 - dr_multi_res$tau_2_true)^2)) cat("DR-Learner RMSE (full sample):

function(y_vec, outcome_label) {   mask_a <- (treatment_lung == 0L) | (treatment_lung == 1L)   mask_b <- (treatment_lung == 0L) | (treatment_lung == 2L)   wa <- as.integer(treatment_lung[mask_a] == 1L)   wb <- as.integer(treatment_lung[mask_b] == 2L)   xa <- X_lung[mask_a, , drop = FALSE]   xb <- X_lung[mask_b, , drop = FALSE]   lx_a <- fit(     XLearner(learner = "xgb", control_name = 0L),     xa, wa, y_vec[mask_a],     nrounds = nrounds_lung_xgb   )   lx_b <- fit(     XLearner(learner = "xgb", control_name = 0L),     xb, wb, y_vec[mask_b],     nrounds = nrounds_lung_xgb   )   list(lx_a = lx_a, lx_b = lx_b, outcome_label = outcome_label) }  lung_shap_fits <- NULL if (!has_ks_lung || !has_sv_lung) {   message("Skipping lung SHAP: install.packages(c(\"kernelshap\", \"shapviz\")) to run this section.") } else {   lung_shap_fits <- list()   for (outcome_nm in c("log_time", "health_status")) {     y_vec <- if (identical(outcome_nm, "log_time")) y_log else y_health     lung_shap_fits[[outcome_nm]] <- lung_shap_one_outcome(y_vec, outcome_nm)   } } n_explain_lung <- min(if (fast_run) 50L else 120L, nrow(X_lung)) bg_size_lung <- min(if (fast_run) 80L else 200L, nrow(X_lung))  if (!is.null(lung_shap_fits)) {   suppressPackageStartupMessages({     library(kernelshap)     library(shapviz)   })   use_future_lung <- requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE)   shap_workers_lung <- if (use_future_lung) {     max(1L, min(4L, future::availableCores() - 1L))   } else {     1L   }   parallel_shap_lung <- use_future_lung && shap_workers_lung > 1L   if (parallel_shap_lung) {     future::plan(future::multisession, workers = shap_workers_lung)     on.exit(future::plan(future::sequential), add = TRUE)   }   shap_parallel_args_lung <- if (parallel_shap_lung) {     list(packages = c("RCausalML", "xgboost"))   } else {     NULL   }    set.seed(2026)   idx_ex <- sample.int(nrow(X_lung), n_explain_lung)   bg_idx <- sample.int(nrow(X_lung), bg_size_lung)   X_explain <- as.data.frame(X_lung[idx_ex, , drop = FALSE])   bg_X_lung <- as.data.frame(X_lung[bg_idx, , drop = FALSE])    for (outcome_nm in names(lung_shap_fits)) {     fits <- lung_shap_fits[[outcome_nm]]     sh_a <- explain_cate(       fits$lx_a,       X = X_explain,       bg_X = bg_X_lung,       use_permshap = TRUE,       verbose = FALSE,       parallel = parallel_shap_lung,       parallel_args = shap_parallel_args_lung     )     sh_b <- explain_cate(       fits$lx_b,       X = X_explain,       bg_X = bg_X_lung,       use_permshap = TRUE,       verbose = FALSE,       parallel = parallel_shap_lung,       parallel_args = shap_parallel_args_lung     )     shp_a <- shapviz(sh_a, X = X_explain)     shp_b <- shapviz(sh_b, X = X_explain)     feat_nm <- colnames(X_explain)     Sa <- as.matrix(sh_a$S)     Sb <- as.matrix(sh_b$S)     colnames(Sa) <- feat_nm     colnames(Sb) <- feat_nm     imp_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(       data.frame(         feature = feat_nm,         mean_abs_shap = colMeans(abs(Sa)),         contrast = "A vs placebo",         stringsAsFactors = FALSE       ),       data.frame(         feature = feat_nm,         mean_abs_shap = colMeans(abs(Sb)),         contrast = "B vs placebo",         stringsAsFactors = FALSE       )     )     p_imp <- ggplot2::ggplot(imp_df, ggplot2::aes(x = reorder(feature, mean_abs_shap), y = mean_abs_shap)) +       ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.75) +       ggplot2::facet_wrap(~contrast, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +       ggplot2::coord_flip() +       ggplot2::labs(         title = paste0("Lung data: mean |SHAP| for predicted CATE (", outcome_nm, ")"),         subtitle = "Per-arm X-Learner (XGBoost); simulated three-arm treatment",         x = NULL,         y = "Mean |SHAP|"       ) +       ggplot2::theme_bw() +       ggplot2::theme(strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"))     print(p_imp)     print(sv_importance(shp_a, kind = "beeswarm") + ggplot2::ggtitle(paste(outcome_nm, ": A vs placebo")))     print(sv_importance(shp_b, kind = "beeswarm") + ggplot2::ggtitle(paste(outcome_nm, ": B vs placebo")))   } }

# Continuous Treatment Generator (Dose-Response) generate_continuous_treatment_data <- function(n = 5000) {   X <- matrix(rnorm(n * 10), nrow = n)   colnames(X) <- paste0("X", 1:10)   D <- pmax(0, rnorm(n, mean = 2 + 1.5*X[,1] - X[,2], sd = 1.2))   mu_0 <- 2*X[,1] - 1.5*X[,2] + X[,4]^2   Y <- mu_0 + 0.8*D + 0.5*X[,1]*D - 0.3*X[,2]*D + 0.05*D^2 + rnorm(n, sd = 1.5)   data.frame(Y, D, as.data.frame(X)) } df_cont <- generate_continuous_treatment_data(5000)

what: Use case: Double machine learning on NMES (DML)
text: reuse subsample (X_meta, d_meta = packyears, y_meta = TOTALEXP) fit partially linear DML ranger nuisances: LinearDML (OLS final stage residual interactions), SparseLinearDML (Lasso final stage), CausalForestDML (grf::causal_forest residuals). three target \(\hat{\theta}(X)\) \(\tilde{Y} \approx \tilde{D}\cdot\theta(X)\) continuous \(\tilde{D}\) (see R/DMLearner.R). ground-truth CATE NMES, compare () ATE large-sample normal CI, (ii) holdout RMSE cross-fitted \(\hat{\mathbb{E}}[Y\mid X]\) 30% test split (models refit 70% train ), (iii) Spearman correlation predicted \(\hat{\theta}(X)\) full subsample (agreement rankings across methods). NMES subsample: Double ML variants — ATE, mean |CATE|, pairwise Spearman correlation predicted CATE. Interpretation: ATE rows aggregate \(\hat{\theta}(X)\); intervals use notebook’s default large-sample standard error mean CATE (debiased DML inference). RMSE_EY_holdout measures well cross-fitted outcome nuisance predicts \(Y\) sample—higher overlap smoother \(\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X]\) often yield lower RMSE. Spearman shows whether heterogeneity rankings agree across linear, sparse, forest final stages.
code: set.seed(2026L) nt_dml <- 220L n_f_dml <- 4L if (!requireNamespace("grf", quietly = TRUE)) {   dml_lin_nmes <- dml_sparse_nmes <- dml_cf_nmes <- NULL   message("Skipping DML comparison: install.packages(\"grf\") for CausalForestDML.") } else {   dml_lin_nmes <- LinearDML(     model_y = "ranger", model_t = "ranger",     n_fold = n_f_dml, seed = 20261L   )   dml_sparse_nmes <- SparseLinearDML(     model_y = "ranger", model_t = "ranger",     alpha = 0.15, n_fold = n_f_dml, seed = 20262L   )   dml_cf_nmes <- CausalForestDML(     model_y = "ranger", model_t = "ranger",     n_fold = n_f_dml, seed = 20263L,     num_trees = 800L, min_node_size = 8L   )   dml_lin_nmes <- fit(dml_lin_nmes, X_meta, d_meta, y_meta, num.trees = nt_dml)   dml_sparse_nmes <- fit(dml_sparse_nmes, X_meta, d_meta, y_meta, num.trees = nt_dml)   # CausalForestDML: grf::causal_forest already receives num.trees from the constructor; passing num.trees   # through ... would duplicate the argument — omit here (ranger nuisances use their defaults).   dml_cf_nmes <- fit(dml_cf_nmes, X_meta, d_meta, y_meta)    ate_lin <- estimate_ate(dml_lin_nmes, X_meta, d_meta, y_meta, return_ci = TRUE, pretrain = TRUE)   ate_spr <- estimate_ate(dml_sparse_nmes, X_meta, d_meta, y_meta, return_ci = TRUE, pretrain = TRUE)   ate_cf <- estimate_ate(dml_cf_nmes, X_meta, d_meta, y_meta, return_ci = TRUE, pretrain = TRUE)    tau_l <- as.numeric(predict(dml_lin_nmes, X_meta))   tau_s <- as.numeric(predict(dml_sparse_nmes, X_meta))   tau_c <- as.numeric(predict(dml_cf_nmes, X_meta))   cors <- matrix(NA_real_, 3L, 3L, dimnames = list(c("LinearDML", "SparseLinearDML", "CausalForestDML"),                                                     c("LinearDML", "SparseLinearDML", "CausalForestDML")))   M <- cbind(tau_l, tau_s, tau_c)   n_complete <- sum(complete.cases(M))   if (n_complete >= 3L) {     for (i in 1:3) for (j in 1:3)       cors[i, j] <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor(M[, i], M[, j], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"))   } else {     warning("Fewer than 3 complete rows in predicted CATE matrix; Spearman correlations set to NA.")   }    tbl_dml_main <- data.frame(     method = c("LinearDML", "SparseLinearDML", "CausalForestDML"),     ATE = c(as.numeric(ate_lin$ate)[1L], as.numeric(ate_spr$ate)[1L], as.numeric(ate_cf$ate)[1L]),     CI_low = c(as.numeric(ate_lin$ate_lb)[1L], as.numeric(ate_spr$ate_lb)[1L], as.numeric(ate_cf$ate_lb)[1L]),     CI_high = c(as.numeric(ate_lin$ate_ub)[1L], as.numeric(ate_spr$ate_ub)[1L], as.numeric(ate_cf$ate_ub)[1L]),     mean_abs_CATE = c(mean(abs(tau_l)), mean(abs(tau_s)), mean(abs(tau_c))),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   )    n_te <- max(30L, floor(0.3 * nrow(X_meta)))   ix_te <- sample.int(nrow(X_meta), n_te)   ix_tr <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(X_meta)), ix_te)   X_tr <- X_meta[ix_tr, , drop = FALSE]   X_te <- X_meta[ix_te, , drop = FALSE]   d_tr <- d_meta[ix_tr]   d_te <- d_meta[ix_te]   y_tr <- y_meta[ix_tr]   y_te <- y_meta[ix_te]    rmse_yhat <- function(est, pass_nt = TRUE) {     est_tr <- if (pass_nt) {       fit(est, X_tr, d_tr, y_tr, num.trees = nt_dml)     } else {       fit(est, X_tr, d_tr, y_tr)     }     comp <- predict(est_tr, X_te, return_components = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)     sqrt(mean((y_te - comp$yhat_c)^2, na.rm = TRUE))   }   # Refit fresh constructors so train-fold fits do not overwrite full-sample objects used for SHAP below   tbl_dml_main$RMSE_EY_holdout <- c(     rmse_yhat(LinearDML(model_y = "ranger", model_t = "ranger", n_fold = n_f_dml, seed = 3031L), TRUE),     rmse_yhat(SparseLinearDML(model_y = "ranger", model_t = "ranger", alpha = 0.15, n_fold = n_f_dml, seed = 3032L), TRUE),     rmse_yhat(CausalForestDML(model_y = "ranger", model_t = "ranger", n_fold = n_f_dml, seed = 3033L,                               num_trees = 800L, min_node_size = 8L), FALSE)   )    knitr::kable(tbl_dml_main, digits = 2)   cat("\nSpearman correlation of predicted CATE (full subsample):\n")   knitr::kable(cors, digits = 3) } Spearman correlation of predicted CATE (full subsample):

set.seed(42) # Optional: tmle package for TMLE-based validation has_tmle <- requireNamespace("tmle", quietly = TRUE) if (!has_tmle) message("Install 'tmle' for TMLE section: install.packages("tmle")") # Optional: MatchIt for LaLonde (Part B) has_matchit <- requireNamespace("MatchIt", quietly = TRUE) if (!has_matchit) message("Install 'MatchIt' for Part B (LaLonde): install.packages("MatchIt")") # Generate synthetic data using mode 1 (same as Python: mode=1, p=10, sigma=5) n_total <- 20000L   # Python uses 1e6; increase (e.g. 100000) for smoother curves p <- 10 sigma <- 5.0 d <- synthetic_data(mode = 1, n = n_total, p = p, sigma = sigma) y <- d$y X <- d$X treatment <- d$w tau <- d$tau e <- d$e # 50/50 train-test split (Python: train_test_split(..., test_size=0.5, random_state=42)) train_frac <- 0.5 n_train <- round(n_total * train_frac) idx <- sample.int(n_total, n_train) X_train   <- X[idx, , drop = FALSE] X_test    <- X[-idx, , drop = FALSE] y_train   <- y[idx] y_test    <- y[-idx] e_train   <- e[idx] e_test    <- e[-idx] treatment_train <- treatment[idx] treatment_test <- treatment[-idx] tau_train <- tau[idx] tau_test  <- tau[-idx] n_test <- nrow(X_test) cat("Train:", n_train, "Test:", n_test, "
") Train: 10000 Test: 10000 learner_x <- XLearner(learner = "ranger") learner_x <- fit(learner_x, X_train, treatment_train, y_train, p = e_train) cate_x_test <- as.vector(predict(learner_x, X_test)) alpha <- 0.5 bins <- 30 par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1)) hist(cate_x_test, col = adjustcolor("steelblue", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA,      main = "Distribution of CATE Predictions by X-Learner and Actual",      xlab = "Individual Treatment Effect (ITE/CATE)", ylab = "# of Samples") hist(tau_test, col = adjustcolor("darkorange", alpha), breaks = bins, border = NA, add = TRUE) legend("topright", legend = c("X-Learner", "Actual"), fill = c("steelblue", "darkorange"), bty = "n") df <- data.frame(   y = y_test,   w = treatment_test,   p = e_test,   tau = tau_test,   X_Learner = cate_x_test,   Actual = tau_test ) # Python: plot(df, outcome_col='y', treatment_col='w', treatment_effect_col='tau') plot_gain(df,           outcome_col = "y",           treatment_col = "w",           treatment_effect_col = "tau",           model_cols = c("X_Learner", "Actual"),           main = "Uplift curve with ground truth",           normalize = TRUE) gain_mat <- get_cumgain(df, outcome_col = "y", treatment_col = "w",                         treatment_effect_col = "tau", normalize = TRUE) n_pts <- nrow(gain_mat) frac <- (0:(n_pts - 1)) / (n_pts - 1) gain_x <- gain_mat[, "X_Learner"] gain_actual <- gain_mat[, "Actual"] # Data without tau so gain uses observed outcome difference (Python: df.drop('tau', axis=1)) df_no_tau <- df[, c("y", "w", "X_Learner", "Actual")] # Mirrors Python: plot(df.drop('tau', axis=1), outcome_col='y', treatment_col='w') plot_gain(df_no_tau,           outcome_col = "y",           treatment_col = "w",           main = "Uplift curve without ground truth (observed outcome difference)") # Add X_test columns as col_0, col_1, ... (Python: inference_cols) inference_cols <- paste0("col_", seq_len(ncol(X_test)) - 1) for (j in seq_len(ncol(X_test)))   df[[inference_cols[j]]] <- X_test[, j] head(df) # ATE via tmle on test set W_df <- as.data.frame(X_test) colnames(W_df) <- paste0("W", seq_len(ncol(W_df))) # Use SL libraries that work with tmle (add SL.ranger if SuperLearner is installed) fit_tmle <- tmle::tmle(   Y = y_test,   A = treatment_test,   W = W_df,   Q.SL.library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm"),   g.SL.library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm") ) ate_tmle <- fit_tmle$estimates$ATE$psi ate_tmle_ci <- fit_tmle$estimates$ATE$CI cat("ATE (TMLE):", round(ate_tmle, 4), "95% CI:", round(ate_tmle_ci, 4), "
") ATE (TMLE): 0.7959 95% CI: 0.4651 1.1267 # Meta-learner ATE on test set (for comparison) ate_x <- estimate_ate(learner_x, X_test, treatment_test, y_test, p = e_test) cat("ATE (X-Learner):", round(ate_x$ate, 4), "95% CI:", round(ate_x$ate_lb, 4), "-", round(ate_x$ate_ub, 4), "
") ATE (X-Learner): 0.6044 95% CI: 0.5201 - 0.6886 # Segment-level TMLE (n_segment=5, like Python get_tmlegain) n_seg_tmle <- 5 seg_size_tmle <- floor(n_test / n_seg_tmle) ord_x <- order(cate_x_test, decreasing = TRUE) tmle_gain_seg <- numeric(n_seg_tmle) for (k in seq_len(n_seg_tmle)) {   idx_k <- ord_x[((k - 1) * seg_size_tmle + 1):(k * seg_size_tmle)]   W_k <- as.data.frame(X_test[idx_k, , drop = FALSE])   colnames(W_k) <- paste0("W", seq_len(ncol(W_k)))   fit_k <- tmle::tmle(     Y = y_test[idx_k],     A = treatment_test[idx_k],     W = W_k,     Q.SL.library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm"),     g.SL.library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm")   )   tmle_gain_seg[k] <- fit_k$estimates$ATE$psi } cum_tmle_gain <- cumsum(tmle_gain_seg * seg_size_tmle) tot_tmle <- cum_tmle_gain[n_seg_tmle] gain_tmle_norm <- if (tot_tmle != 0) cum_tmle_gain / tot_tmle else cum_tmle_gain frac_tmle <- (1:n_seg_tmle) / n_seg_tmle plot(frac_tmle, gain_tmle_norm, type = "b", pch = 19, lwd = 2, col = "purple",      xlab = "Fraction of samples (sorted by X-Learner CATE)",      ylab = "Cumulative gain (TMLE segment ATE, normalized)",      main = "Uplift curve with TMLE as proxy for ground truth") lines(frac, gain_x, lwd = 2, col = "steelblue", lty = 2) legend("bottomright", legend = c("TMLE (segment ATE)", "X-Learner (true τ)"),        col = c("purple", "steelblue"), lty = c(1, 2), lwd = 2, pch = c(19, NA), bty = "n") # AUUC = mean of normalized cumulative gain (Python auuc_score(..., normalize=True)) auuc_scores <- colMeans(gain_mat[, c("X_Learner", "Actual")]) cat("AUUC (X-Learner, with true τ):", round(auuc_scores["X_Learner"], 4), "
") AUUC (X-Learner, with true τ): 0.5354 cat("AUUC (Optimal by true τ):", round(auuc_scores["Actual"], 4), "
") AUUC (Optimal by true τ): 0.6168 # AUUC with TMLE: area under normalized segment TMLE gain (Python auuc_score(..., tmle=True)) auuc_tmle_x <- mean(gain_tmle_norm) cat("AUUC (X-Learner, TMLE segment gain):", round(auuc_tmle_x, 4), "
") AUUC (X-Learner, TMLE segment gain): 0.6652 # Qini with TMLE: cumulative incremental outcome by segment (Python get_tmleqini(..., ci=False)) n_cum <- c(0, seg_size_tmle * (1:n_seg_tmle)) qini_tmle <- c(0, cum_tmle_gain) plot(n_cum, qini_tmle, type = "b", pch = 19, lwd = 2, col = "purple",      xlab = "# of samples (sorted by X-Learner CATE)",      ylab = "Cumulative incremental outcome (TMLE)",      main = "Qini curve with TMLE as proxy for ground truth") # With ground truth (Python qini_score(..., treatment_effect_col='tau')) qini_scores <- qini_score(df,                           outcome_col = "y",                           treatment_col = "w",                           treatment_effect_col = "tau",                           model_cols = c("X_Learner", "Actual")) print(round(qini_scores, 2)) X_Learner    Actual   26592203  30635223 # Approximate Qini score from TMLE segments (trapezoidal area under qini_tmle vs n_cum) qini_tmle_score <- sum(diff(n_cum) * (qini_tmle[-1] + qini_tmle[-length(qini_tmle)]) / 2) cat("Qini score (TMLE segment curve):", round(qini_tmle_score, 2), "
") Qini score (TMLE segment curve): 41690584 # Mirrors Python: plot(df, kind='qini', outcome_col='y', treatment_col='w', treatment_effect_col='tau') plot_qini(df,           outcome_col = "y",           treatment_col = "w",           treatment_effect_col = "tau",           model_cols = c("X_Learner", "Actual"),           main = "Qini curve (with ground truth)")

text: Doubly Robust Learner (DR-Learner) meta-learner estimating Conditional Average Treatment Effect observational data discrete treatments. belongs family doubly robust estimators: combining outcome model propensity score model, remains consistent either — necessarily — correctly specified. nuisance models converge sufficiently fast rates, DR-Learner achieves \(\sqrt{n}\)-consistency asymptotic normality CATE, enabling valid confidence intervals hypothesis tests available standard meta-learners. DR-Learner applies : treatment \(T\) discrete, \(T \\{0, 1, \dots, K-1\}\) designated reference arm \(T = 0\). Confounders observed — possibly high-dimensional — covariate vector \((X, W)\). Unconfoundedness holds: \(Y(t) \perp T \mid X, W\) \(t\). target estimand active arm \(t \geq 1\) contrast control: \[\tau_t(x) = \mathbb{E}[Y(t) - Y(0) \mid X = x]\] DR-Learner requires two nuisance objects, estimated using flexible ML algorithms: Arm-specific outcome models: \(\hat{g}_t(X, W) \approx \mathbb{E}[Y \mid T = t, X, W]\) arm \(t\). Propensity scores: \(\hat{p}_t(X, W) \approx P(T = t \mid X, W)\) arm \(t\). critical implementation detail cross-fitting (also called sample splitting), RCausalML performs 3-fold rotation default, following Kennedy (2020). sample partitioned \(K\) folds; fold, nuisance models trained remaining \(K-1\) folds used construct pseudo-outcomes held-fold. rotation ensures observations used fit nuisance models never ones used construct pseudo-outcomes fit final CATE model. (generic estimate_ate dispatches DR DML methods appropriate). Useful arguments: control_name (default 0), n_fold (default 3; internally capped 3 DR rotation), seed, ate_alpha. DRLearner, can set control_outcome_learner, treatment_outcome_learner, treatment_effect_learner separately. Ellipsis ... passed ranger, xgboost, etc. linear DR learners, coef() intercept() summarize final-stage slopes intercept (averaged across cross-fitting folds applicable).

what: Part A: DR Learners with Sythetic Data
text: First show examples DR learners {RCausaML} shared synthetic data-generating process (DGP) binary treatment linear CATE. DGP includes 5 effect modifiers (X1–X5) 3 confounders (W1–W3), treatment assignment depending confounders outcome depending confounders effect modifiers. true CATE linear X1 , allowing us evaluate well DR learner captures structure.  Forest DR-Learner: predicted CATE vs true driver X1 (training sample). Overlap check using fitted propensity:  Propensity score distribution treatment group. simulation linear X1 ; columns enter confounding may appear small estimated slopes. Requires xgboost package. Example: flexible nuisances linear CATE surface.
code:
set.seed(42)  n <- 2000 X_mod <- matrix(rnorm(n * 5), n, 5) W <- matrix(rnorm(n * 3), n, 3) colnames(X_mod) <- paste0("X", 1:5) colnames(W) <- paste0("W", 1:3)  # Full covariate matrix passed to learners (modifiers + confounders) X <- cbind(X_mod, W) colnames(X) <- c(colnames(X_mod), colnames(W))  propensity <- 1 / (1 + exp(-W[, 1] - 0.5 * W[, 2])) treatment <- rbinom(n, 1L, propensity)  true_cate <- 1 + 0.8 * X_mod[, 1] Y <- as.vector(2 + 0.5 * W %*% c(1, -1, 0.5) + true_cate * treatment + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5))  mean_ate_true <- mean(true_cate) dr_forest <- ForestDRLearner(control_name = 0L, n_fold = 3L, seed = 42) dr_forest <- fit(dr_forest, X, treatment, Y, num.trees = 300L)  cate_forest <- predict(dr_forest, X) ate_dr_f <- estimate_ate(dr_forest, X, treatment, Y, pretrain = TRUE, seed = 42)  cat("Mean predicted CATE:", round(mean(cate_forest), 4),     "| True mean CATE:", round(mean_ate_true, 4), "
") Mean predicted CATE: 0.9742 | True mean CATE: 0.9875 cat("estimate_ate (point, CI):", round(ate_dr_f$ate, 4),     "[", round(ate_dr_f$ate_lb, 4), ",", round(ate_dr_f$ate_ub, 4), "]
") estimate_ate (point, CI): 0.9742 [ 0.9226 , 1.0258 ] phat <- dr_forest$propensity[["1"]] df_plot <- data.frame(   X1 = X_mod[, 1],   cate_hat = as.numeric(cate_forest),   true_cate = true_cate )  df_ord <- df_plot[order(df_plot$X1), ] ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = X1, y = cate_hat)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.15, color = "steelblue") +   geom_smooth(se = TRUE, color = "darkblue", linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_line(aes(x = X1, y = true_cate), color = "black", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.6, data = df_ord) +   labs(x = expression(X[1]), y = "Predicted CATE", title = "ForestDRLearner") +   theme_minimal() ggplot(data.frame(p = phat, T = factor(treatment)), aes(x = p, fill = T)) +   geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +   labs(x = expression(hat(p)(X)), title = "Overlap (ForestDRLearner propensity)") +   theme_minimal() dr_lin <- LinearDRLearner(   model_propensity = "ranger",   model_regression = "ranger",   control_name = 0L,   n_fold = 3L,   seed = 42 ) dr_lin <- fit(dr_lin, X, treatment, Y, num.trees = 200L)  cate_lin <- predict(dr_lin, X)  cat("Mean predicted CATE (linear DR):", round(mean(cate_lin), 4),     "| True mean CATE:", round(mean_ate_true, 4), "
") Mean predicted CATE (linear DR): 1.0153 | True mean CATE: 0.9875 # Final-stage linear CATE coefficients (slopes on columns of X) cat("coef() — slopes:
") coef() — slopes: print(round(coef(dr_lin), 4)) X1      X2      X3      X4      X5      W1      W2      W3   0.7634  0.0291 -0.0418  0.0187 -0.0094  0.0107 -0.0133  0.0051 cat("intercept():
") intercept(): print(round(intercept(dr_lin), 4)) [1] 1.0285 dr_sparse <- SparseLinearDRLearner(   model_propensity = "ranger",   model_regression = "ranger",   alpha = 1,   control_name = 0L,   n_fold = 3L,   seed = 42 ) dr_sparse <- fit(dr_sparse, X, treatment, Y, num.trees = 200L)  cate_sparse <- predict(dr_sparse, X) cat("Mean predicted CATE (sparse linear DR):", round(mean(cate_sparse), 4), "
") Mean predicted CATE (sparse linear DR): 0.9714 cat("Non-zero coef() entries (approximate selection):
") Non-zero coef() entries (approximate selection): print(round(coef(dr_sparse), 4)) X1     X2     X3     X4     X5     W1     W2     W3  0.1483 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 if (requireNamespace("xgboost", quietly = TRUE)) {   dr_xgb <- XGBDRLearner(control_name = 0L, n_fold = 3L, seed = 42)   dr_xgb <- fit(dr_xgb, X, treatment, Y, nrounds = 80L)   cate_xgb <- predict(dr_xgb, X)   cat("Mean predicted CATE (XGB DR):", round(mean(cate_xgb), 4), "
") } dr_mixed <- DRLearner(   learner = "ranger",   control_outcome_learner = "ranger",   treatment_outcome_learner = "ranger",   treatment_effect_learner = "lm",   control_name = 0L,   n_fold = 3L,   seed = 42 ) dr_mixed <- fit(dr_mixed, X, treatment, Y, num.trees = 200L) cate_mixed <- predict(dr_mixed, X) cat("Mean predicted CATE (mixed DR):", round(mean(cate_mixed), 4), "
") Mean predicted CATE (mixed DR): 0.9747 dml_lin <- LinearDML(   model_y = "ranger",   model_t = "ranger",   control_name = 0L,   n_fold = 3L,   seed = 42 ) dml_lin <- fit(dml_lin, X, treatment, Y, num.trees = 200L) cate_dml_lin <- predict(dml_lin, X) cat("Mean predicted CATE (LinearDML):", round(mean(cate_dml_lin), 4), "
") Mean predicted CATE (LinearDML): 0.9894 comparison <- data.frame(   method = c(     "True mean CATE",     "ForestDRLearner",     "LinearDRLearner",     "SparseLinearDRLearner",     "DRLearner (RF + lm tau)",     "LinearDML"   ),   mean_CATE_or_target = c(     mean_ate_true,     mean(cate_forest),     mean(cate_lin),     mean(cate_sparse),     mean(cate_mixed),     mean(cate_dml_lin)   ) ) comparison$mean_CATE_or_target <- round(comparison$mean_CATE_or_target, 4) print(comparison, row.names = FALSE) method mean_CATE_or_target           True mean CATE              0.9875          ForestDRLearner              0.9742          LinearDRLearner              1.0153    SparseLinearDRLearner              0.9714  DRLearner (RF + lm tau)              0.9747                LinearDML              0.9894

what: Part B: Use case — abortion data
text: apply meta-learner API abortion dataset causaldata (state–year units; outcome lnr, logged gonorrhea rate among 15–19 year olds; treatment early repeal abortion prohibition). load raw table load_causaldata("abortion")$data, restrict ages 15–19, encode treatment binary factor levels "Control" (early repeal) "Treated" (early repeal). Internally, RCausalML maps factor numeric codes (1 = Control, 2 = Treated levels = c("Control", "Treated")), every meta-learner constructed control_name = 1L. fit learner training rows report () mean predicted CATE held-test covariates X_ab_te (heterogeneity summary new units) (ii) ATE training sample using estimate_ate(..., pretrain = TRUE) (point estimate normal approx. interval DR learner’s ate_alpha). Runs xgboost installed; otherwise single table row records skipped.  attribute predicted \(\hat{\tau}(X)\) fitted DR learner covariates using permutation SHAP (explain_cate(..., use_permshap = TRUE)). Background explanation rows drawn training split (X_ab_tr). predict() DR learners evaluates fitted nuisance final-stage CATE model newdata, kernelshap requires. Parallel workers use future / parallel pattern binary-treatment notebook, ranger, glmnet, xgboost included parallel_args$packages relevant.       CATE Treated minus Control log outcome scale encoding; intervals follow package’s DR ATE routine (see estimate_ate.DRLearner). DR learners RCausalML (R/meta_learners.R) implement cross-fitted, doubly robust meta-learning several final-stage choices: forests (ForestDRLearner), OLS (LinearDRLearner), Lasso (SparseLinearDRLearner), XGBoost (XGBDRLearner), fully custom mix via DRLearner(). DML (R/DMLearner.R) residualizes \(Y\) \(T\) (vector \(T\)) fits second-stage model heterogeneous effects; CausalForestDML connects pipeline grf. Use estimate_ate() simple average effect summary analytic (bootstrap) uncertainty DR side; DML dispatch provides ATE helper. References: Kennedy (2020) [[45]]; Foster et al. (2019); Chernozhukov et al. (2018) DML. EconML: DR, DML.

text: Uplift trees estimate causal effect treatment individual — whether outcome likely, whether specific action caused . standard predictive model asks “convert?”, uplift model asks: “convert intervention?” estimand Conditional Average Treatment Effect: \[\tau(x) = P(Y = 1 \mid T = 1, X = x) - P(Y = 1 \mid T = 0, X = x)\] \(T = 1\) denotes treatment, \(T = 0\) control, \(Y\) binary outcome, \(x\) individual’s covariate vector. Individuals fall four behavioral segments based potential outcomes: Persuadables (\(\tau(x) > 0\)): primary targeting objective — buy treatment. Sure Things (\(\tau(x) \approx 0\)): buy regardless; treatment wasted. Lost Causes (\(\tau(x) \approx 0\)): buy regardless. --Disturbs (\(\tau(x) < 0\)): treatment actively suppresses conversion. Standard predictive models conflate Sure Things Persuadables. Uplift trees separate targeting \(\tau(x)\) directly. node, algorithm finds split maximizes treatment effect divergence across child nodes. general gain formula : \[\text{gain} = \frac{n_\ell}{n}\, D(p^\ell, q^\ell) + \frac{n_r}{n}\, D(p^r, q^r) - D(p, q)\] \(p = P(Y \mid T=1)\), \(q = P(Y \mid T=0)\), \(D(\cdot,\cdot)\) divergence measure. Three divergence criteria supported: multi-arm settings, Contextual Treatment Selection (CTS; Zhao et al., 2017) replaces divergence maximization reward-based criterion scores split gain expected outcome optimal arm assignment: \[\hat{\Delta}_\mu(s) = \hat{p}(\phi_\ell \mid \phi)\max_t \hat{\mu}_t(\phi_\ell) + \hat{p}(\phi_r \mid \phi)\max_t \hat{\mu}_t(\phi_r) - \max_t \hat{\mu}_t(\phi)\] Three adjustments stabilize splits reduce bias: Gain normalization: divides \(H(T \mid \phi)\) correct treatment imbalance within node. Sample-size penalty: multiplies \(\frac{n_\ell n_r}{(n_\ell + n_r)^2}\), penalizing lopsided splits. Treatment-imbalance penalty: subtracts \(\alpha \sum_t |\hat{\pi}_\phi(t) - \hat{\pi}(t)|\) discourage splits driven local assignment drift rather genuine effect heterogeneity.
