text: Intervention analysis assesses effects actively changing (intervening ) one variables within system. -operation \((X = x)\) forces variable take specific value evaluates change propagates causal graph affect variables. Average Treatment Effect (ATE) measures expected difference outcome variable due intervention: \[\text{ATE} = \mathbb{E}[Y \mid (X = 1)] - \mathbb{E}[Y \mid (X = -1)].\]
code: source_name <- "Energy" target_name <- "Industrials" source_idx  <- which(VAR_NAMES == source_name) target_idx  <- which(VAR_NAMES == target_name)  # DECI ATE via Monte-Carlo averaging over the decoder ate_val <- ate_deci(   object    = deci_fit,   newdata   = X_val,   source    = source_idx,   target    = target_idx,   do_values = c(-1.0, 1.0),   n_samples = min(200L, nrow(X_val)) ) cat(sprintf("Estimated ATE of do(%s) on %s (DECI): %.4f\n",             source_name, target_name, ate_val)) Estimated ATE of do(Energy) on Industrials (DECI): -0.0049 # DeepSCM intervention: compare predicted target under low vs. high intervention n_int <- min(128L, nrow(X_val)) int_result <- intervene_deep_scm(   object     = deep_scm_fit,   newdata    = X_val[seq_len(n_int), , ],   target_var = source_idx,   do_values  = c(-1.0, 1.0) )  scm_delta <- int_result$delta[target_idx] cat(sprintf("DeepSCM intervention delta on %s: %.4f\n", target_name, scm_delta)) DeepSCM intervention delta on Industrials: 0.5169 diff_vec <- int_result$pred_high[, target_idx] - int_result$pred_low[, target_idx]  ggplot(data.frame(delta = diff_vec), aes(x = delta)) +   geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#7570b3", colour = "white", alpha = 0.85) +   geom_vline(xintercept = mean(diff_vec), colour = "#e7298a", linewidth = 1,              linetype = "dashed") +   annotate("text",            x     = mean(diff_vec) + 0.02 * diff(range(diff_vec)),            y     = Inf, vjust = 2,            label = sprintf("Mean delta = %.4f", mean(diff_vec)),            colour = "#e7298a", size = 3.5) +   labs(     title = sprintf(       "DeepSCM Intervention: do(%s) → %s response distribution",       source_name, target_name     ),     x = sprintf("Predicted Δ%s under do(%s=+1) − do(%s=−1)",                 target_name, source_name, source_name),     y = "Count"   ) +   theme_minimal()

diff_vec <- int_result$pred_high[, target_idx] - int_result$pred_low[, target_idx]  ggplot(data.frame(delta = diff_vec), aes(x = delta)) +   geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#7570b3", colour = "white", alpha = 0.85) +   geom_vline(xintercept = mean(diff_vec), colour = "#e7298a", linewidth = 1,              linetype = "dashed") +   annotate("text",            x     = mean(diff_vec) + 0.02 * diff(range(diff_vec)),            y     = Inf, vjust = 2,            label = sprintf("Mean delta = %.4f", mean(diff_vec)),            colour = "#e7298a", size = 3.5) +   labs(     title = sprintf(       "DeepSCM Intervention: do(%s) → %s response distribution",       source_name, target_name     ),     x = sprintf("Predicted Δ%s under do(%s=+1) − do(%s=−1)",                 target_name, source_name, source_name),     y = "Count"   ) +   theme_minimal()

text: DYNOTEARS extends NOTEARS-style continuous optimization time-series causal discovery modelling lagged dependencies enforcing acyclicity learned structure. lag order \(p\), formulation : \[X_t = W^{(0)}X_t + \sum_{k=1}^{p} W^{(k)} X_{t-k} + \epsilon_t,\] \(W^{(0)}\) captures -time (instantaneous) effects \(W^{(k)}\) captures directed lag-\(k\) effects. augmented-Lagrangian objective penalizes reconstruction error, L1 sparsity, DAG violation simultaneously. useful practice: Produces interpretable directed graphs explicit lag structure. Provides DAG-regularized structure learning differentiable framework. Useful structure-learning rigor needed beyond purely predictive models.

text: TCDF (Nauta et al., 2019) uses depthwise separable causal convolutions + self-attention discover time-delayed causal relationships. Key ideas: Dilated causal convolutions: receptive field grows exponentially depth without data leakage — output depends past inputs. Attention mechanism: scores input channels (variables) contribute target variable. Causal discovery: target \(Y_i\), trains separate network; variables high attention weights declared causal parents. convolution dilation \(r\): \[\text{Conv}(x, t) = \sum_{k=0}^{K-1} w_k \cdot x(t - r \cdot k)\] Causal mask ensures \(x(t - r \cdot k)\) uses past values (\(k \geq 0\), never \(k < 0\)). Transformer three structural modifications enforce causal reasoning: Autoregressive masking: upper-triangular mask attention position \(t\) attends positions \(\leq t\). Inter-variable attention head: separate attention heads dedicated cross-variable influence, whose weights extracted causal graph. Positional encoding: sinusoidal temporal embeddings encode lag distance. causal attention output: \[\text{CausalAttn}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M_{\text{causal}}\right) V\] \(M_{\text{causal}}[,j] = -\infty\) \(j > \), else \(0\). TFT (Lim et al., 2021, Google) state---art architecture interpretable multi-horizon forecasting. causal structure comes : Variable Selection Networks (VSN): soft gating selects input variables relevant time step — directly interpretable variable-level causal weights. Gated Residual Networks (GRN): nonlinear transformation skip connections gating stable training. Multi-head attention interpretable weights: attention across time steps, averaged across heads produce temporal importance scores. TFT architecture flow:
code: Input variables       │       ▼ Variable Selection Network  ← learns which vars matter (causal weights)       │       ▼ LSTM Encoder/Decoder        ← captures local temporal dynamics       │       ▼ Multi-Head Self-Attention   ← captures long-range dependencies       │       ▼ Gated Residual + LayerNorm  ← stabilize gradients       │       ▼ Output Head                 ← one-step-ahead forecast per variable

text: section downloads S&P 500 sector ETF prices (universe used companion notebooks), converts standardized log-returns, builds lagged input/output arrays training. Note: online market data unavailable, notebook automatically falls back synthetic demo data downstream cells remain runnable.

TICKERS <- c(   "XLF" = "Financials",   "XLE" = "Energy",   "XLK" = "Technology",   "XLV" = "Healthcare",   "XLI" = "Industrials",   "XLY" = "ConsumerDisc",   "XLP" = "ConsumerStap",   "XLU" = "Utilities" )  fetch_close_prices <- function(tickers, start = "2018-01-01", end = "2024-01-01") {   tryCatch({     raw <- tidyquant::tq_get(names(tickers), get = "stock.prices",                               from = start, to = end, complete_cases = TRUE)     if (is.null(raw) || nrow(raw) == 0) return(NULL)     raw |>       dplyr::select(symbol, date, adjusted) |>       tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = symbol, values_from = adjusted) |>       dplyr::arrange(date) |>       tidyr::drop_na()   }, error = function(e) NULL) }  close_wide <- fetch_close_prices(TICKERS)  if (is.null(close_wide) || nrow(close_wide) < 30) {   message("Warning: market data unavailable; using synthetic demo data.")   set.seed(42)   n_steps <- 1600L   d_syn   <- length(TICKERS)   A_syn   <- matrix(0, d_syn, d_syn)   for (i in seq_len(d_syn)) {     A_syn[i, i] <- 0.45     if (i > 1)             A_syn[i, i - 1] <- 0.25     if (i > 2 && i %% 2 == 1) A_syn[i, i - 2] <- 0.15   }   x_syn <- matrix(0, n_steps, d_syn)   x_syn[1, ] <- rnorm(d_syn)   noise_syn  <- 0.15 * matrix(rnorm(n_steps * d_syn), n_steps, d_syn)   for (t in seq(2L, n_steps)) x_syn[t, ] <- x_syn[t - 1L, ] %*% t(A_syn) + noise_syn[t, ]   returns_df <- as.data.frame(x_syn)   colnames(returns_df) <- unname(TICKERS)   data_np <- scale(x_syn) } else {   price_mat <- as.matrix(close_wide[, names(TICKERS)])   log_ret   <- log(price_mat[-1L, ] / price_mat[-nrow(price_mat), ])   colnames(log_ret) <- unname(TICKERS[colnames(price_mat)])   returns_df <- as.data.frame(log_ret)   data_np    <- scale(log_ret) }  VAR_NAMES <- colnames(data_np) d         <- ncol(data_np) Tt        <- nrow(data_np)  cat(sprintf("d=%d variables, T=%d
", d, Tt)) d=8 variables, T=1508 cat("Variables:", paste(VAR_NAMES, collapse = ", "), "
") Variables: Financials, Energy, Technology, Healthcare, Industrials, ConsumerDisc, ConsumerStap, Utilities LAG   <- 20L AHEAD <- 1L  build_lag_dataset <- function(data, lag, ahead = 1L) {   N     <- nrow(data) - lag - ahead + 1L   x_seq <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(N, lag, ncol(data)))   y_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = N, ncol = ncol(data))   for (t in seq_len(N)) {     x_seq[t, , ] <- data[t:(t + lag - 1L), , drop = FALSE]     y_mat[t,  ]  <- data[t + lag + ahead - 1L, ]   }   list(x_seq = x_seq, y_mat = y_mat) }  lag_data <- build_lag_dataset(data_np, LAG, AHEAD) X_seq    <- lag_data$x_seq Y_mat    <- lag_data$y_mat  split  <- floor(0.8 * nrow(X_seq)) X_tr   <- X_seq[seq_len(split), , ] X_val  <- X_seq[(split + 1L):nrow(X_seq), , ] Y_tr   <- Y_mat[seq_len(split), ] Y_val  <- Y_mat[(split + 1L):nrow(Y_mat), ]  cat(sprintf("Train: (%d, %d, %d)  Val: (%d, %d, %d)
",             dim(X_tr)[1], dim(X_tr)[2], dim(X_tr)[3],             dim(X_val)[1], dim(X_val)[2], dim(X_val)[3])) Train: (1190, 20, 8)  Val: (298, 20, 8)

text: section, describe three attention-based neural network models implemented RCausalML fitted using attn_causal_model(). architecture designed multivariate time-series causal inference. foundational building block TCDFNet causal dilated convolutional block: 1-D convolution dilation \(2^\) layer \(\) (exponentially growing receptive field). Left-padding ensures future leakage. LayerNorm features + GELU nonlinearity. R (via torch), internal .deepnet_attn_tcdf_net() constructor stacks n_layers blocks, applies linear attention projection head two-layer MLP prediction head. R implementation CausalTransformer: Input projection: linear map \(d\) variables \(d_{\text{model}}\) dimensions. Sinusoidal positional encoding: adds temporal position information. Causal TransformerEncoder: standard multi-head self-attention upper-triangular mask (causal masking). Cross-variable attention head: separate nn_multihead_attention() computes inter-variable attention — averaged weights form causal matrix. Per-variable GRN + linear heads: one Gated Residual Network linear layer per output variable. R implementation TFTNet: Variable Selection Network (VSN): per-variable GRNs produce embeddings; context GRN produces soft selection weights — weights variable-level causal importances. Temporal projection + LSTM encoder: projects \(d\) variables \(d_{\text{model}}\) runs LSTM. Causal multi-head attention: LSTM outputs attend causal mask. Final GRN + linear head: combines LSTM context VSN context GRN prediction head. Causal matrix: outer product mean VSN weights \(\rightarrow\) variable--variable causal matrix.

text: section downloads S&P 500 sector ETF prices (universe used companion notebooks), converts standardized log-returns, builds lagged input/output arrays training, derives volatility-spike intervention proxy (top-25% rolling-variance days). Note: online market data unavailable, notebook automatically falls back synthetic demo data downstream cells remain runnable.
code:
TICKERS <- c(   "XLF" = "Financials",   "XLE" = "Energy",   "XLK" = "Technology",   "XLV" = "Healthcare",   "XLI" = "Industrials",   "XLY" = "ConsumerDisc",   "XLP" = "ConsumerStap",   "XLU" = "Utilities" )  fetch_close_prices <- function(tickers, start = "2018-01-01", end = "2024-01-01") {   tryCatch({     raw <- tidyquant::tq_get(names(tickers), get = "stock.prices",                               from = start, to = end, complete_cases = TRUE)     if (is.null(raw) || nrow(raw) == 0) return(NULL)     raw |>       dplyr::select(symbol, date, adjusted) |>       tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = symbol, values_from = adjusted) |>       dplyr::arrange(date) |>       tidyr::drop_na()   }, error = function(e) NULL) }  close_wide <- fetch_close_prices(TICKERS)  if (is.null(close_wide) || nrow(close_wide) < 30) {   message("Warning: market data unavailable; using synthetic demo data.")   set.seed(42)   n_steps <- 1600L   d_syn   <- length(TICKERS)   A_syn   <- matrix(0, d_syn, d_syn)   for (i in seq_len(d_syn)) {     A_syn[i, i] <- 0.45     if (i > 1)                 A_syn[i, i - 1] <- 0.25     if (i > 2 && i %% 2 == 1) A_syn[i, i - 2] <- 0.15   }   x_syn <- matrix(0, n_steps, d_syn)   x_syn[1, ] <- rnorm(d_syn)   noise_syn  <- 0.15 * matrix(rnorm(n_steps * d_syn), n_steps, d_syn)   for (t in seq(2L, n_steps)) x_syn[t, ] <- x_syn[t - 1L, ] %*% t(A_syn) + noise_syn[t, ]   returns_df <- as.data.frame(x_syn)   colnames(returns_df) <- unname(TICKERS)   data_np <- scale(x_syn) } else {   price_mat <- as.matrix(close_wide[, names(TICKERS)])   log_ret   <- log(price_mat[-1L, ] / price_mat[-nrow(price_mat), ])   colnames(log_ret) <- unname(TICKERS[colnames(price_mat)])   returns_df <- as.data.frame(log_ret)   data_np    <- scale(log_ret) }  VAR_NAMES <- colnames(data_np) d         <- ncol(data_np) Tt        <- nrow(data_np)  cat(sprintf("d=%d variables, T=%d
", d, Tt)) d=8 variables, T=1508 cat("Variables:", paste(VAR_NAMES, collapse = ", "), "
") Variables: Financials, Energy, Technology, Healthcare, Industrials, ConsumerDisc, ConsumerStap, Utilities LAG   <- 20L AHEAD <- 1L  build_lag_dataset <- function(data, lag, ahead = 1L) {   N     <- nrow(data) - lag - ahead + 1L   x_seq <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(N, lag, ncol(data)))   y_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = N, ncol = ncol(data))   for (t in seq_len(N)) {     x_seq[t, , ] <- data[t:(t + lag - 1L), , drop = FALSE]     y_mat[t,  ]  <- data[t + lag + ahead - 1L, ]   }   list(x_seq = x_seq, y_mat = y_mat) }  lag_data <- build_lag_dataset(data_np, LAG, AHEAD) X_seq    <- lag_data$x_seq Y_mat    <- lag_data$y_mat  split  <- floor(0.8 * nrow(X_seq)) X_tr   <- X_seq[seq_len(split), , ] X_val  <- X_seq[(split + 1L):nrow(X_seq), , ] Y_tr   <- Y_mat[seq_len(split), ] Y_val  <- Y_mat[(split + 1L):nrow(Y_mat), ]  cat(sprintf("Train: (%d, %d, %d)  Val: (%d, %d, %d)
",             dim(X_tr)[1], dim(X_tr)[2], dim(X_tr)[3],             dim(X_val)[1], dim(X_val)[2], dim(X_val)[3])) Train: (1190, 20, 8)  Val: (298, 20, 8) # Intervention proxy: top-25% rolling-variance days (volatility spikes) roll_sd <- zoo::rollapply(data_np, width = 10, FUN = sd, by.column = TRUE,                           fill = NA, align = "right") if (!requireNamespace("zoo", quietly = TRUE)) {   roll_sd <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(data_np), d)   for (j in seq_len(d)) {     for (t in seq(10L, nrow(data_np)))       roll_sd[t, j] <- sd(data_np[(t - 9L):t, j])   } } global_sd  <- rowMeans(roll_sd, na.rm = TRUE) global_sd[is.na(global_sd)] <- 0 threshold  <- quantile(global_sd, 0.75) I_raw      <- as.numeric(global_sd > threshold)  cat(sprintf("Intervention rate: %.1f%%
", 100 * mean(I_raw))) Intervention rate: 25.0% cat(sprintf("Intervention vector length: %d
", length(I_raw))) Intervention vector length: 1508

text: section, describe three RNN/LSTM-based causal neural network models implemented RCausalML fitted using rnn_causal_model(). architecture designed multivariate time-series causal inference. R implementation CausalLSTM RCausalML: LearnableCausalMask: \(d \times d\) sigmoid-parameterized adjacency matrix diagonal fixed 1 (self-causality) L1 sparsity penalty -diagonal entries. Per-variable LSTMs: \(d\) variables nn_lstm fed masked input \(G_{,:} \odot x_t\). Output heads: two-layer MLP (hidden→hidden/2→1) per variable producing one-step-ahead forecasts. Sparsity loss: added MSE training, promoting parsimonious causal graphs. Causal matrix: soft mask \(G\) (hardened version) extracted evaluation time. R implementation RETAIN RCausalML: Embedding layer: linear projection timestep’s features hidden_alpha dimensions. Reverse-time processing: input embedded sequence flipped time GRU processing. Alpha GRU + head: GRU reversed embeddings → scalar softmax attention weights \(\alpha_t\) (one per timestep). Beta GRU + head: second GRU → tanh-transformed feature weights \(\beta_t \\mathbb{R}^d\) (one vector per timestep). Context aggregation: \(c = \sum_t \alpha_t \cdot (\beta_t \odot x_t)\) → output head. Causal matrix: aggregated \(|W| \cdot |\beta|\) attribution averaged validation batches. R implementation InterventionAwareRNN RCausalML: RegimeDetector: GRU processes input sequence → softmax \(K\) regime logits. Regime embedding: linear projection regime probabilities → dense regime_dim-vector, repeated along sequence length. Intervention projection: scalar intervention indicator \(I_t\) → dense regime_dim-vector per timestep. Augmented LSTM: input \([x_t; r_t; I_t] \\mathbb{R}^{d + 2 \cdot \text{regime\_dim}}\) step. Prediction head: GELU-activated MLP last LSTM state → \(d\)-vector forecast. Causal matrix: regime-probability-softmax-weighted average learnable \(\Psi_k\) matrices.

plot_causal_heatmap <- function(C, title, var_names) {   A <- as.matrix(C)   diag(A) <- NA_real_   rownames(A) <- var_names   colnames(A) <- var_names   df <- reshape2::melt(A, na.rm = TRUE)   colnames(df) <- c("Target", "Source", "Weight")   df$Target <- factor(df$Target, levels = rev(var_names))   df$Source <- factor(df$Source, levels = var_names)   ggplot(df, aes(x = Source, y = Target, fill = Weight)) +     geom_tile(colour = "white") +     geom_text(aes(label = round(Weight, 2)), size = 2.5, colour = "black") +     scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#2C7BB6",                         na.value = "grey90", name = "Weight") +     labs(title = title, x = "Source (cause)", y = "Target (effect)") +     theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +     theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)) }  p_lstm   <- plot_causal_heatmap(C_lstm,   "CausalLSTM — Learned Mask",          VAR_NAMES) p_retain <- plot_causal_heatmap(C_retain, "RETAIN — Beta Attribution",           VAR_NAMES) p_interv <- plot_causal_heatmap(C_interv, "InterventionRNN — Regime-Avg Matrix", VAR_NAMES)  patchwork::wrap_plots(p_lstm, p_retain, p_interv, ncol = 3)

draw_rnn_igraph <- function(C, title, var_names, threshold = 0.12,                              node_colour = "steelblue") {   M     <- as.matrix(C)   M[is.na(M)] <- 0.0   A_bin <- (M > threshold) * 1L   diag(A_bin) <- 0L   g <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(     A_bin, mode = "directed", weighted = NULL, diag = FALSE   )   igraph::V(g)$name        <- var_names   igraph::V(g)$color       <- node_colour   igraph::V(g)$label       <- var_names   igraph::V(g)$size        <- 28   igraph::V(g)$label.color <- "white"   igraph::V(g)$label.cex   <- 0.8   igraph::E(g)$color       <- "grey50"   igraph::E(g)$arrow.size  <- 0.6    old_par <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0))   plot(g,        layout = igraph::layout_in_circle(g),        main   = title,        vertex.frame.color = "white")   par(old_par) }  par(mfrow = c(1, 3)) draw_rnn_igraph(C_lstm,   "CausalLSTM (threshold > 0.12)",     VAR_NAMES, 0.12, "steelblue") draw_rnn_igraph(C_retain, "RETAIN (threshold > 0.12)",         VAR_NAMES, 0.12, "darkorange") draw_rnn_igraph(C_interv, "InterventionRNN (threshold > 0.12)",VAR_NAMES, 0.12, "mediumpurple") par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

graph_stats_rnn <- function(C, threshold = 0.12, name = "") {   M     <- as.matrix(C)   M[is.na(M)] <- 0.0   A_bin <- (M > threshold) * 1L   diag(A_bin) <- 0L   g    <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(     A_bin, mode = "directed", weighted = NULL, diag = FALSE   )   d_n  <- igraph::gorder(g)   e_n  <- igraph::gsize(g)   dens <- if (d_n > 1) e_n / (d_n * (d_n - 1)) else 0.0   data.frame(     model          = name,     nodes          = d_n,     edges          = e_n,     density        = round(dens, 4),     is_dag         = igraph::is_dag(g),     max_in_degree  = if (d_n > 0) max(igraph::degree(g, mode = "in"))  else 0L,     max_out_degree = if (d_n > 0) max(igraph::degree(g, mode = "out")) else 0L   ) }  stats_all <- do.call(rbind, list(   graph_stats_rnn(C_lstm,   0.12, "CausalLSTM"),   graph_stats_rnn(C_retain, 0.12, "RETAIN"),   graph_stats_rnn(C_interv, 0.12, "InterventionRNN") )) rownames(stats_all) <- NULL  cat("Graph statistics (threshold = 0.12):\n") Graph statistics (threshold = 0.12): print(stats_all) model nodes edges density is_dag max_in_degree max_out_degree 1      CausalLSTM     8    56       1  FALSE             7              7 2          RETAIN     8     0       0   TRUE             0              0 3 InterventionRNN     8    56       1  FALSE             7              7

text: RETAIN’s dual-channel attention produces interpretable attribution scores. extract alpha (temporal importance) beta (variable importance) validation set visualise .
code: retain_mod <- rnn_fit$models[["retain"]] retain_mod$eval()  dev_use <- if (is.null(device_use)) "cpu" else device_use n_plot  <- min(200L, nrow(X_val)) x_sub   <- torch::torch_tensor(X_val[seq_len(n_plot), , ],                                 dtype  = torch::torch_float32(),                                 device = dev_use)  retain_out <- torch::with_no_grad({ retain_mod$forward(x_sub) })  # Alpha: temporal attention (n_plot x LAG) alpha_mat <- as.matrix(retain_out$alpha$cpu()) alpha_mean <- colMeans(alpha_mat)  # Beta: variable attention averaged over time (n_plot x d) beta_3d  <- retain_out$beta$abs()$cpu() beta_mat <- as.matrix(beta_3d$mean(dim = 2L))  # (n_plot, d) beta_mean <- colMeans(beta_mat)  # --- Plot 1: Mean temporal attention across validation set --- alpha_df <- data.frame(   lag    = seq_len(LAG),   weight = alpha_mean )  p_alpha <- ggplot(alpha_df, aes(x = lag, y = weight)) +   geom_col(fill = "#d95f02", alpha = 0.8) +   labs(     title = "RETAIN: Mean Temporal Attention (α)",     x     = "Lag (steps back from t)",     y     = "Mean α weight"   ) +   theme_minimal()  # --- Plot 2: Mean variable attention --- beta_df <- data.frame(   variable = VAR_NAMES,   weight   = beta_mean )  p_beta <- ggplot(beta_df, aes(x = reorder(variable, -weight), y = weight, fill = variable)) +   geom_col(show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 0.85) +   scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +   labs(     title = "RETAIN: Mean Variable Attention (|β|)",     x     = "Variable",     y     = "Mean |β| weight"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))  patchwork::wrap_plots(p_alpha, p_beta, ncol = 2)

text: Intervention-Aware RNN compare predictions zero-intervention vs. observed intervention signal validation set.
code: interv_mod <- rnn_fit$models[["intervention_rnn"]] interv_mod$eval()  dev_use <- if (is.null(device_use)) "cpu" else device_use n_plot  <- min(200L, nrow(X_val)) x_sub_t <- torch::torch_tensor(X_val[seq_len(n_plot), , ],                                 dtype   = torch::torch_float32(),                                 device  = dev_use)  # Reconstruct the intervention window for validation samples using X_val rows n_full <- nrow(X_val) # X_val rows come from positions (split+1):(N) of X_seq, which map to time # indices (split+1):(N) in the lagged dataset, i.e. original rows (split+1+LAG-1)... I_val_win <- matrix(0.0, n_full, LAG) offset <- split  # first validation sample starts at row split+1 in X_seq for (t in seq_len(n_full)) {   ts   <- offset + t            # position in X_seq (1-indexed)   i_st <- ts                    # original series index for the lag window start   i_en <- ts + LAG - 1L   if (i_en <= length(I_raw))     I_val_win[t, ] <- I_raw[i_st:i_en] } I_val_win <- pmin(pmax(I_val_win, 0), 1)  i_obs_t  <- torch::torch_tensor(I_val_win[seq_len(n_plot), ],                                  dtype  = torch::torch_float32(),                                  device = dev_use) i_zero_t <- torch::torch_zeros_like(i_obs_t)  out_obs  <- torch::with_no_grad({ interv_mod$forward(x_sub_t, interv = i_obs_t)  }) out_zero <- torch::with_no_grad({ interv_mod$forward(x_sub_t, interv = i_zero_t) })  pred_obs  <- as.matrix(out_obs$pred$cpu()) pred_zero <- as.matrix(out_zero$pred$cpu())  # Average absolute prediction difference per variable diff_df <- data.frame(   variable = VAR_NAMES,   avg_diff = colMeans(abs(pred_obs - pred_zero)) )  ggplot(diff_df, aes(x = reorder(variable, -avg_diff), y = avg_diff, fill = variable)) +   geom_col(show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 0.85) +   scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +   labs(     title = "Intervention Effect: Mean |Prediction Change| under Observed vs. Zero Intervention",     x     = "Sector variable",     y     = "Mean |Δ prediction|"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

Learns probabilistic Bernoulli graph edges \(q(G) \approx \prod_{ij} \mathrm{Bernoulli}(\pi_{ij})\) jointly imputes missing values forecasting. composite ELBO-style loss : \[\mathcal{L} = \underbrace{\mathbb{E}[\log p(X_{\mathrm{obs}} \mid G, X_{\mathrm{miss}})]}_{\text{reconstruction}} + \underbrace{\mathbb{E}[\log p(X_{\mathrm{miss}} \mid G)]}_{\text{imputation}} - \underbrace{\mathrm{KL}[q(G) \| p(G)]}_{\text{graph prior}}\]

text: section downloads S&P 500 sector ETF prices, converts standardized log-returns, builds lagged input/output arrays, injects synthetic missingness (15 %) CUTS+ demonstration. Note: online market data unavailable, notebook automatically falls back synthetic demo data downstream cells remain runnable.

TICKERS <- c(   "XLF" = "Financials",   "XLE" = "Energy",   "XLK" = "Technology",   "XLV" = "Healthcare",   "XLI" = "Industrials",   "XLY" = "ConsumerDisc",   "XLP" = "ConsumerStap",   "XLU" = "Utilities" )  fetch_close_prices <- function(tickers, start = "2018-01-01", end = "2024-01-01") {   tryCatch({     raw <- tidyquant::tq_get(names(tickers), get = "stock.prices",                               from = start, to = end, complete_cases = TRUE)     if (is.null(raw) || nrow(raw) == 0) return(NULL)     raw |>       dplyr::select(symbol, date, adjusted) |>       tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = symbol, values_from = adjusted) |>       dplyr::arrange(date) |>       tidyr::drop_na()   }, error = function(e) NULL) }  close_wide <- fetch_close_prices(TICKERS)  if (is.null(close_wide) || nrow(close_wide) < 30) {   message("Warning: market data unavailable; using synthetic demo data.")   set.seed(42)   n_steps <- 1600L   d_syn   <- length(TICKERS)   A_syn   <- matrix(0, d_syn, d_syn)   for (i in seq_len(d_syn)) {     A_syn[i, i] <- 0.45     if (i > 1)                 A_syn[i, i - 1] <- 0.25     if (i > 2 && i %% 2 == 1) A_syn[i, i - 2] <- 0.15   }   x_syn      <- matrix(0, n_steps, d_syn)   x_syn[1, ] <- rnorm(d_syn)   noise_syn  <- 0.15 * matrix(rnorm(n_steps * d_syn), n_steps, d_syn)   for (t in seq(2L, n_steps)) x_syn[t, ] <- x_syn[t - 1L, ] %*% t(A_syn) + noise_syn[t, ]   returns_df <- as.data.frame(x_syn)   colnames(returns_df) <- unname(TICKERS)   data_np    <- scale(x_syn) } else {   price_mat  <- as.matrix(close_wide[, names(TICKERS)])   log_ret    <- log(price_mat[-1L, ] / price_mat[-nrow(price_mat), ])   colnames(log_ret) <- unname(TICKERS[colnames(price_mat)])   returns_df <- as.data.frame(log_ret)   data_np    <- scale(log_ret) }  VAR_NAMES <- colnames(data_np) d         <- ncol(data_np) Tt        <- nrow(data_np)  cat(sprintf("d=%d variables, T=%d
", d, Tt)) d=8 variables, T=1508 cat("Variables:", paste(VAR_NAMES, collapse = ", "), "
") Variables: Financials, Energy, Technology, Healthcare, Industrials, ConsumerDisc, ConsumerStap, Utilities LAG   <- 10L AHEAD <- 1L  build_lag_dataset <- function(data, lag, ahead = 1L) {   N     <- nrow(data) - lag - ahead + 1L   x_seq <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(N, lag, ncol(data)))   y_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = N, ncol = ncol(data))   for (t in seq_len(N)) {     x_seq[t, , ] <- data[t:(t + lag - 1L), , drop = FALSE]     y_mat[t,  ]  <- data[t + lag + ahead - 1L, ]   }   list(x_seq = x_seq, y_mat = y_mat) }  lag_data <- build_lag_dataset(data_np, LAG, AHEAD) X_seq    <- lag_data$x_seq Y_mat    <- lag_data$y_mat  split  <- floor(0.8 * nrow(X_seq)) X_tr   <- X_seq[seq_len(split), , ] X_val  <- X_seq[(split + 1L):nrow(X_seq), , ] Y_tr   <- Y_mat[seq_len(split), ] Y_val  <- Y_mat[(split + 1L):nrow(Y_mat), ]  cat(sprintf("Train: (%d, %d, %d)  Val: (%d, %d, %d)
",             dim(X_tr)[1], dim(X_tr)[2], dim(X_tr)[3],             dim(X_val)[1], dim(X_val)[2], dim(X_val)[3])) Train: (1198, 10, 8)  Val: (300, 10, 8) # Inject 15 % synthetic missingness for CUTS+ demo (same as Python notebook) set.seed(0L) MISS_RATE <- 0.15 miss_mask <- array(runif(prod(dim(X_seq))) < MISS_RATE, dim = dim(X_seq)) X_miss    <- X_seq X_miss[miss_mask] <- 0.0 X_miss_tr  <- X_miss[seq_len(split), , ] X_miss_val <- X_miss[(split + 1L):nrow(X_seq), , ]  cat(sprintf("Missing rate: %.1f%%
", 100 * mean(miss_mask))) Missing rate: 15.1% cat(sprintf("Missing tensor shape: (%d, %d, %d)
", dim(X_miss)[1], dim(X_miss)[2], dim(X_miss)[3])) Missing tensor shape: (1498, 10, 8)

text: three architectures implemented R torch nn_module objects inside RCausalML accessible single entry-point gnn_causal_model(). GVARGraphLearner: \(p\) lag-specific \((d \times d)\) sigmoid-parameterised adjacency matrices; diagonal forced zero (self-loops); L1 sparsity penalty. GVARMessagePass (×2): per-lag linear transform + ReLU → batch-matmul \(^{(k)}\) → concatenate → aggregate linear layer. Prediction head: input-projected features (1 → hidden) pass two stacked GNN layers two-layer GELU MLP producing \(d\)-vector forecasts. Losses: MSE + sparsity (L1) + DAG (NOTEARS acyclicity). Per-variable GRU encoder: variable’s \(T\)-step sequence encoded hidden-dim state. CausalGraphLearner: bilinear edge scoring temporal summaries → soft DAG \(\hat{} \[0,1]^{d \times d}\). EdgeConvLayer (×n_gnn_layers): concatenates source/target features + edge weight → two-layer MLP → GRU update → layer norm. Losses: MSE + DAG acyclicity + L1 sparsity. Losses: MSE + DAG acyclicity + KL(\(q(G) \| \text{Bernoulli}(0.1)\))

Classical synthetic control estimates treated unit’s counterfactual using weighted controls: \[\hat{Y}_t^{(0)} = \sum_{j \\text{controls}} w_j Y_{t,j}, \quad w_j \ge 0,\; \sum_j w_j = 1\] DeepSynth replaces fixed linear weights neural representation learning scaled dot-product attention donor series: \[w_j = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{q \cdot k_j}{\sqrt{d}}\right), \quad \hat{Y}^{(0)} = \sum_j w_j v_j\] CRN uses recurrent representations adversarial balancing reduce treatment-assignment bias: \[\min_{\text{enc, pred}} \max_D \; \mathcal{L}_{\text{pred}} - \lambda\mathcal{L}_{\text{disc}}\] discriminator \(D\) tries predict treatment encoded representation \(r\); encoder penalised making \(r\) informative \(T\), producing balanced representation. G-Net learns sequential generative models covariates outcomes, rolls forward interventions: \[\mathbb{E}[Y_t(\bar{})] = \int \prod_{k=1}^{t} p(X_k\mid\bar{X}_{k-1},\bar{}_{k-1}=\bar{}_{k-1})\,p(Y_t\mid\bar{X}_t,\bar{}_t=\bar{}_t)\,d\bar{X}\] use RCausalML’s counterfactual_model() function (convenience wrappers deep_synth_model(), crn_model(), gnet_model()) fit three architectures S&P 500 sector ETF daily log-return data (2018–2024). section downloads S&P 500 sector ETF prices, computes standardized log-returns, defines binary treatment (Technology sector top-quartile return days) scalar outcome (Financials next-step return). synthetic fallback provided market data unavailable. Factual head: \(\text{MLP}(z_{\text{treated}} \| T_{t+1}) \\hat{Y}^{\text{factual}}\). Counterfactual head: \(\text{MLP}(z_{cf}) \\hat{Y}^{(0)}\). ITE: \(\hat{Y}^{\text{factual}} - \hat{Y}^{(0)}\). text: Time-varying confounders create feedback loops: \[X_t \rightarrow T_t \rightarrow Y_{t+1} \rightarrow X_{t+1} \rightarrow T_{t+1} \rightarrow \cdots\] \(X_t\) can : confounder (affects treatment outcome), intermediate variable (affected prior treatment). breaks naive regression assumptions motivates causal sequence models.

Classical synthetic control estimates treated unit’s counterfactual using weighted controls: \[\hat{Y}_t^{(0)} = \sum_{j \\text{controls}} w_j Y_{t,j}, \quad w_j \ge 0,\; \sum_j w_j = 1\] DeepSynth replaces fixed linear weights neural representation learning scaled dot-product attention donor series: \[w_j = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{q \cdot k_j}{\sqrt{d}}\right), \quad \hat{Y}^{(0)} = \sum_j w_j v_j\] CRN uses recurrent representations adversarial balancing reduce treatment-assignment bias: \[\min_{\text{enc, pred}} \max_D \; \mathcal{L}_{\text{pred}} - \lambda\mathcal{L}_{\text{disc}}\] discriminator \(D\) tries predict treatment encoded representation \(r\); encoder penalised making \(r\) informative \(T\), producing balanced representation. G-Net learns sequential generative models covariates outcomes, rolls forward interventions: \[\mathbb{E}[Y_t(\bar{})] = \int \prod_{k=1}^{t} p(X_k\mid\bar{X}_{k-1},\bar{}_{k-1}=\bar{}_{k-1})\,p(Y_t\mid\bar{X}_t,\bar{}_t=\bar{}_t)\,d\bar{X}\]

text: section downloads S&P 500 sector ETF prices, computes standardized log-returns, defines binary treatment (Technology sector top-quartile return days) scalar outcome (Financials next-step return). synthetic fallback provided market data unavailable. Note: online market data unavailable, notebook automatically falls back synthetic demo data downstream cells remain runnable.

TICKERS <- c(   "XLF" = "Financials",   "XLE" = "Energy",   "XLK" = "Technology",   "XLV" = "Healthcare",   "XLI" = "Industrials",   "XLY" = "ConsumerDisc",   "XLP" = "ConsumerStap",   "XLU" = "Utilities" )  fetch_close_prices <- function(tickers, start = "2018-01-01", end = "2024-01-01") {   tryCatch({     raw <- tidyquant::tq_get(names(tickers), get = "stock.prices",                               from = start, to = end, complete_cases = TRUE)     if (is.null(raw) || nrow(raw) == 0) return(NULL)     raw |>       dplyr::select(symbol, date, adjusted) |>       tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = symbol, values_from = adjusted) |>       dplyr::arrange(date) |>       tidyr::drop_na()   }, error = function(e) NULL) }  close_wide <- fetch_close_prices(TICKERS)  if (is.null(close_wide) || nrow(close_wide) < 30) {   message("Warning: market data unavailable; using synthetic demo data.")   set.seed(42)   n_steps <- 1200L   d_syn   <- length(TICKERS)   # Correlated synthetic returns with a latent market factor   market   <- matrix(rnorm(n_steps), n_steps, 1) * 0.8   loading  <- seq(0.5, 1.1, length.out = d_syn)   idio     <- matrix(rnorm(n_steps * d_syn) * 0.6, n_steps, d_syn)   data_np  <- sweep(market %*% t(loading), 2, rep(0, d_syn)) + idio   colnames(data_np) <- unname(TICKERS) } else {   price_mat  <- as.matrix(close_wide[, names(TICKERS)])   log_ret    <- log(price_mat[-1L, ] / price_mat[-nrow(price_mat), ])   colnames(log_ret) <- unname(TICKERS[colnames(price_mat)])   data_np    <- scale(log_ret) }  VAR_NAMES <- colnames(data_np) d         <- ncol(data_np) Tt        <- nrow(data_np)  cat(sprintf("d=%d variables, T=%d
", d, Tt)) d=8 variables, T=1508 cat("Variables:", paste(VAR_NAMES, collapse = ", "), "

text: three architectures implemented R torch nn_module objects inside RCausalML accessible single entry-point counterfactual_model(). SharedEncoder: 2-layer GRU (input_dim → latent_dim) + FC layer → ReLU. Donor pool: columns except treatment outcome variables; donor encoded key/value. Scaled dot-product attention: query (treated) × keys (donors) → softmax weights → weighted donor summary \(z_{cf}\). Factual head: \(\text{MLP}(z_{\text{treated}} \| T_{t+1}) \\hat{Y}^{\text{factual}}\). Counterfactual head: \(\text{MLP}(z_{cf}) \\hat{Y}^{(0)}\). ITE: \(\hat{Y}^{\text{factual}} - \hat{Y}^{(0)}\). Encoder: 2-layer GRU \((x, T_{\text{hist}}, y_{\text{lag}})\) → representation \(r\) via LayerNorm + Tanh. Discriminator: MLP predicts \(T\) \(r\); adversarial loss penalises encoder encoding treatment. Decoder: \(\text{MLP}(r \| \text{}(T)) \\hat{Y}\); counterfactuals \(\text{}(T=0)\) \(\text{}(T=1)\). Loss: \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{MSE}} - \lambda_{\text{adv}} \mathcal{L}_{\text{BCE}}(D(r), T)\). Counterfactuals \(\hat{Y}(0)\) \(\hat{Y}(1)\) computed substituting \(\text{}(T=0)\) \(\text{}(T=1)\) heads.

# Helper: safely convert a torch tensor (or NULL) to numeric vector .t2r <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) NULL else as.numeric(x$cpu())  # Helper: collect pred, Y(0), Y(1), ITE from each fitted module # DeepSynth uses `ycounter` for Y(0) and `pred` as factual proxy for Y(1); # CRN and GNet expose `y0` and `y1` directly. collect_cf <- function(fit_obj, model_name, batch_size = 256L) {   mod <- fit_obj$models[[model_name]]   if (is.null(mod)) stop("Model not fitted: ", model_name)   vd  <- fit_obj$val_data   dev <- fit_obj$device   mod$eval()    N        <- dim(vd$X)[1L]   idx_list <- split(seq_len(N), ceiling(seq_len(N) / batch_size))    preds <- y0s <- y1s <- ites <- numeric(0)   for (idx in idx_list) {     Xb  <- torch::torch_tensor(       vd$X[idx, , , drop = FALSE],       dtype = torch::torch_float32(), device = dev)     Thb <- torch::torch_tensor(       vd$T_hist[idx, , drop = FALSE],       dtype = torch::torch_float32(), device = dev)     Tnb <- torch::torch_tensor(       vd$T_next[idx],       dtype = torch::torch_float32(), device = dev)      out <- mod$forward(Xb, Thb, Tnb)      # Resolve Y(0) and Y(1): DeepSynth uses 'ycounter'; CRN/GNet use 'y0','y1'     y0_t  <- if (!is.null(out[["y0"]]))       out[["y0"]]              else if (!is.null(out[["ycounter"]])) out[["ycounter"]]              else out[["pred"]]     y1_t  <- if (!is.null(out[["y1"]]))  out[["y1"]]              else out[["pred"]]      preds <- c(preds, .t2r(out[["pred"]]))     y0s   <- c(y0s,   .t2r(y0_t))     y1s   <- c(y1s,   .t2r(y1_t))     ites  <- c(ites,  .t2r(out[["ite"]]))   }   list(pred = preds, y0 = y0s, y1 = y1s, ite = ites) }  pred_ds  <- collect_cf(cf_fit, "deepsynth") pred_crn <- collect_cf(cf_fit, "crn") pred_gn  <- collect_cf(cf_fit, "gnet")  vd    <- cf_fit$val_data n_val <- length(vd$Y_next) cat(sprintf("Validation observations: %d

notebook, explored estimation individual average treatment effects (ITE ATE) context counterfactual reasoning causal inference, using three deep learning architectures — DeepSynth, CRN, G-Net — via RCausalML’s unified counterfactual_model() interface S&P 500 sector ETF data. Key Findings: three models achieve comparable validation MSE, demonstrating explicit causal constraints adversarial balancing need hurt predictive performance. DeepSynth leverages donor similarity via attention, making closest classical synthetic control deep learning framework. CRN explicitly models treatment-confounding feedback adversarial representation balancing, producing balanced latent space suitable -calculus interventions. G-Net supports flexible policy simulations jointly learning covariate outcome transition models, enabling sequential counterfactual rollouts. Conclusions Recommendations: Deep counterfactual models unify temporal representation learning potential-outcomes estimation, offering richer modeling power purely linear baselines. Comparison ITE distributions ATE estimates across models provides useful robustness check: large disagreements suggest unresolved confounding model misspecification. robust application: validate identification assumptions (unmeasured confounders, positivity, consistency), apply sensitivity analyses, use bootstrap confidence intervals treatment effect estimates. work include larger financial universes, formal bootstrap uncertainty ATE/ITE, integration intervention-based validation, doubly-robust estimation strategies.

title: RCausalML 0.1.9
text: Three new model families converted Python (Pearl’s SCM hierarchy — association, intervention, counterfactual) two graph-utility functions: DeepSCM (deep_scm()): Fixed-graph Structural Causal Model. variable’s structural equation small MLP (StructuralEquationNet) conditioned graph-parents per-variable latent noise vector inferred variational encoder (NoiseEncoder). Training minimises ELBO-style objective (MSE reconstruction + KL). Supports predict.deep_scm() intervene_deep_scm() -calculus interventions (returns predictions low/high values mean delta). Adjacency matrix can supplied derived correlation heuristic. CamelCase alias: deepSCM(). DECI (deci_model()): Deep End--end Causal Inference. Jointly learns soft causal adjacency matrix (DECIAdjacency) nonlinear structural equations (DECIEncoder + DECIDecoder) lagged time-series windows. Uses NOTEARS acyclicity penalty  plus KL L1 sparsity ELBO objective. Returns A_soft A_binary (thresholded). Supports predict.deci_model() ate_deci() Monte-Carlo average treatment effect estimation. CamelCase alias: deciModel(). DynoTEARS (dynotears()): Lagged causal discovery multivariate time series. Learns lag-specific weight matrices  augmented-Lagrangian DAG constraint , L1 sparsity, progressive rho/alpha updates. Returns A_binary, W_agg, training diagnostics (train_losses, dag_vals). Supports predict.dynotears(). CamelCase alias: dynoTEARS(). evaluate_graph_recovery(A_true, A_pred, name): Computes TP, FP, FN, Precision, Recall, F1, Structural Hamming Distance (SHD) predicted binary adjacency matrix ground-truth DAG. plot_scm_dag(, var_names, title): Visualises weighted binary adjacency matrix heatmap (ggplot2 + reshape2 available, base-graphics fallback). Diagonal entries masked.

title: RCausalML 0.1.9
text: Causal XGBoost (R/causalXGBoost.R): CXGBoost R6 class implementing two-head DragonNet-style masked-MSE causal outcome model XGBoost ranger propensity scorer. New methods: fit(), predict(), summary(), evaluate() (PEHE + ATE vs ground-truth), plot_importance() (ggplot2 variable-importance chart), save_model() / load_model(), clone_reset(). Exported evaluation metrics PEHE() ATE() accept matrix vector calling conventions. Bug fixes vs v1.0: Hessian always > 0, ranger column selection .max, verbose fully respected parallel workers, XGBoost label flattening. Exported: CXGBoost, PEHE, ATE, ATE_error, run_example. Multi-arm Causal Boosting (R/multi_arm_causal_boost.R): MultiArmCausalBoost R6 class extending binary CXGBoost K ≥ 2 treatment arms. Fits separate XGBoost outcome models per arm multiclass ranger propensity forest. Supports univariate multivariate Y, factor treatment, NA median imputation, treatment contrast reports relative chosen baseline arm. Methods: fit(), predict(), predict_ate(), summary(), plot_importance(), save() / load(). Exported: MultiArmCausalBoost, multi_arm_PEHE, multi_arm_ATE, load_multi_arm_causal_boost, save_multi_arm_causal_boost, run_multi_arm_causal_boost_example. Interventional Causal Representation Learning (R/interventionalCRL.R): InterventionalCRL torch nn_module — environment-conditioned VAE two-hidden-layer encoder/decoder analytically tractable KL divergence q(z|x,e) environment prior p(z|e). Designed binary Morgan-fingerprint inputs (Bernoulli BCE reconstruction). interventional_elbo_loss() computes negative ELBO (BCE + KL) scalar tensor. Optional device auto-selection (CUDA / CPU). Exported via @export tempoCausalVAE.R (TemporalCausalVAE, temporal_causal_loss). Temporal Causal VAE (R/tempoCausalVAE.R): TemporalCausalVAE torch nn_module — GRU encoder/decoder learned latent_dim × latent_dim causal adjacency matrix, NOTEARS-style DAG acyclicity penalty, L1 sparsity adjacency. temporal_causal_loss() computes combined ELBO + DAG + sparsity loss. Beta-VAE KL weighting (beta) separate adjacency penalty weight (gamma) configurable. Exported: TemporalCausalVAE, temporal_causal_loss. Temporal Causal Discovery Framework (R/temporalCausaDiscovery.R): R/torch port TCDF (Nauta et al., https://github.com/M-Nauta/TCDF). Implements depthwise causal TCN building blocks (TCDF_chomp1d, TCDF_first_block, TCDF_temporal_block, TCDF_last_block, TCDF_depthwise_net) TCDF_ADDSTCN attention-based dilated TCN channel-wise causal discovery multivariate time series. Requires torch.
